This article explains the ways the thyroid can go wrong and when you should get checked."}}, {"id": "OIiqZz15Vh", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does the thyroid gland do?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "aqSwxm5B_R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck. It makes hormones that control the metabolism of almost every part of the body. When it does not work properly — making either too much or too little hormone — it can affect many body systems at once."}}, {"id": "y1RNzCzdUn", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism): what are the symptoms?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "tU2OHsLEo4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This happens when the thyroid makes too much hormone. Common symptoms are:"}}, {"id": "noHSWe8GC2", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Weight loss even though you eat more or the same", "Palpitations or an unusually fast heartbeat", "Shaky hands and heavy sweating", "Anxiety and trouble sleeping", "Feeling unusually hot", "Lighter or shorter periods"]}}, {"id": "X5MovnEbKe", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism): what are the symptoms?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "nsj6SYDxKM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This happens when the thyroid makes too little hormone. It is the most common thyroid condition. Common symptoms are:"}}, {"id": "TMfnjNgtAi", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Fatigue and tiring easily", "Weight gain without eating more", "Feeling unusually cold", "Constipation, dry skin and hair loss", "Poorer memory and low mood", "Goitre (an enlarged thyroid gland)"]}}, {"id": "WfYz8ZDOdv", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why do so many people not realise they have a thyroid problem?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "WEg_IC5NvV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The worrying part is that thyroid symptoms often look like everyday health problems or simply getting older, so many people never think of their thyroid. A single symptom may not mean much, but if you have several together, you should have a blood test to check your thyroid hormone levels."}}, {"id": "1iLAIT0-Ec", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: go to hospital immediately", "level": 2}}, {"id": "gJG8lS9Etv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although very rare, severe complications of both types can be life-threatening. Go to hospital immediately if you have:"}}, {"id": "qYdTM1xWQ5", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["High fever, a very fast heartbeat, agitation or confusion in someone with an overactive thyroid (possible thyroid storm)", "Feeling extremely cold and very drowsy, to the point of losing consciousness, in someone with an underactive thyroid (possible myxoedema coma)"]}}, {"id": "YZOdIA39_I", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ccCxWaCT6I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An underactive thyroid is treated with a daily thyroid hormone replacement tablet, which is safe and effective at the right dose. An overactive thyroid has several treatment options, such as anti-thyroid medicine, radioactive iodine or surgery, depending on the cause and what suits each person."}}, {"id": "DwMg3gFIm7", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Thyroid checks and care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "7J07vmn6YI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess symptoms that may be thyroid-related and arrange blood tests to confirm. If you need to see an endocrinologist, we will refer you appropriately."}}, {"id": "_GTpdrFth1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "JzJisAnF1v", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "WgK7WzNGmg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I found a lump in my neck. Should I see a doctor quickly?
Yes, see a doctor for an assessment. Most lumps are not cancer, but every lump should be properly checked."}}, {"id": "MGymtA89sa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need to take medicine for life if I have an underactive thyroid?
Most people need long-term treatment and some need it for life, but the medicine is safe and effective when taken at the dose your doctor prescribes."}}, {"id": "eqwW8LqOS-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does weight going up and down always mean a thyroid problem?
Not always — weight changes have many causes. But if you also have other symptoms, such as palpitations or feeling unusually cold, you should have a blood test."}}, {"id": "0hK07K3DBI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is thyroid disease genetic?
It can run in families in some cases, especially autoimmune thyroid disease. If a family member has thyroid disease, be especially alert."}}, {"id": "Gjm6Ug512m", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "nmxwhF7ha0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Thyroid disease includes an overactive and an underactive thyroid. Their symptoms are opposite, but both can affect the body a great deal. Because the symptoms often look like ordinary health problems, many people do not know they have it. If you have several symptoms together — tiring easily, weight changes, palpitations, or feeling unusually hot or cold — get a blood test soon."}}, {"id": "ldoxChdcyQ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "b7kyrDhBRT", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic Health System – Thyroid disease: Symptoms, treatment", "Mayo Clinic Health System – Do not blame your thyroid", "Mayo Clinic – Hyperthyroidism: Symptoms & causes"]}}, {"id": "-BPMl50VCM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. {"time": 1788314410906, "blocks": [{"id": "u8tRlYf6Xp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Acne is not just a teenage problem. Many adults still have ongoing acne, or even get it for the first time as adults. This article explains what causes acne, how severe it can be, how to look after your skin and when to see a dermatologist."}}, {"id": "ck78QrL__W", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What causes acne?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "yyqk2SLEv6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Acne happens when hair follicles become blocked with oil (sebum) and dead skin cells. When a blocked follicle collects bacteria, it becomes inflamed, forming red spots, whiteheads or blackheads. Acne usually appears on the face, forehead, chest, upper back and shoulders."}}, {"id": "JQbLMLYlTP", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Levels of acne severity", "level": 2}}, {"id": "4zV7573TkY", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mild: mostly whiteheads and blackheads, with a few red spots or pustules", "Moderate: more red spots and pustules, mostly on the face", "Moderately severe: many red spots and pustules, with occasional inflamed lumps", "Severe: many deep cysts or nodules, with a risk of scarring"]}}, {"id": "74qKsTu9jP", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common causes", "level": 2}}, {"id": "BI-RKHxoM1", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Hormonal changes, especially in the teenage years, before a period or during pregnancy", "Genetics", "Some skincare products or cosmetics that clog pores", "Stress", "In adults who suddenly develop severe acne for the first time, it can sometimes be linked to another health condition that should be checked"]}}, {"id": "nX3ngG6dF7", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to look after your skin", "level": 2}}, {"id": "kRDK2GsQrf", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Wash your face twice a day with a gentle cleanser, without scrubbing hard", "Choose skincare and cosmetics labelled non-comedogenic (won’t clog pores)", "Avoid squeezing or picking spots, as this increases the risk of scars", "Use products containing benzoyl peroxide or azelaic acid, following basic guidance"]}}, {"id": "hiY466iogy", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a dermatologist?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "mKODNEz1SJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If over-the-counter products have not helped within 3–4 months, or your acne is getting worse — for example with deep inflamed lumps or cysts — see a dermatologist for more effective treatment. You should also see a doctor if acne is seriously affecting your mood, such as causing stress or anxiety."}}, {"id": "XShcdwl8qb", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Acne care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "dxM0sD1E7c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine your skin, advise on acne care and consider suitable medicine based on how severe your acne is. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "Jbr9_ZapYw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "yYKhXdvIXw", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "-VLH0MKBbD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I squeeze my own spots?
It is best not to, as it increases the risk of infection and scarring. Let a doctor or skin professional deal with them properly."}}, {"id": "GoZCpdqlWZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can acne go away on its own without treatment?
Mild acne sometimes improves by itself, but in most cases the right products help it clear faster and reduce the risk of scars."}}, {"id": "1q9cFmUoCU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is it normal to get acne for the first time as an adult?
It can happen, especially due to hormonal changes. But if severe acne appears suddenly in adulthood, talk to a doctor to check for other possible causes."}}, {"id": "GkKW4h1FxS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do fried food and chocolate really cause acne?
The link between diet and acne is less clear than the role of hormones and genetics. But if you notice more spots after certain foods, you can try avoiding them."}}, {"id": "tHWlsZNjed", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "OQMfUmE2OL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Acne is caused by blocked pores combined with bacterial inflammation, and it can occur at any age, not just in teenagers. Basic skincare with the right products helps many people, but if it does not improve or gets worse, see a dermatologist for more effective treatment before it leaves permanent scars."}}, {"id": "ky9a34ljEw", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "tdZq8-QElT", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Cleveland Clinic – Acne: Types, Causes, Treatment & Prevention", "Mayo Clinic News Network – Home Remedies: All about acne", "Mayo Clinic News Network – Understanding adult acne"]}}, {"id": "oP_urVoRRZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. See a dermatologist if your acne does not improve or gets worse."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1787795670630, "blocks": [{"id": "yxg_9clrnh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sudden pain in the ankle or big toe at night, so bad you can hardly walk — many people do not realise this is the classic sign of gout, one of the most common types of arthritis, especially in men. This article covers the causes, symptoms and self-care to lower the risk of further attacks."}}, {"id": "0CleGtEK-B", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is gout?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "HEoPtETwGo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Gout is caused by uric acid crystals building up in a joint. When there is too much uric acid in the blood, sharp crystals settle in the joints and cause sudden inflammation, with pain, swelling, redness and heat. It most often starts in the big toe, but can also affect the ankle, knee or fingers."}}, {"id": "08jz5cqovk", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who is at risk of gout?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "CQUtPMqmMk", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Men are about 3 times more likely than women to get gout, especially after age 40", "Women after menopause, as the protective effect of oestrogen falls", "People who are overweight or obese", "People who eat a lot of high-purine foods such as organ meats, some seafood and red meat, or who regularly drink alcohol, especially beer", "People taking diuretics (water pills) for high blood pressure"]}}, {"id": "PzyPxSDoR7", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "nALc3lS2ye", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Sudden, severe joint pain, often at night", "Swelling, redness and heat around the affected joint", "Extreme tenderness — even a light touch hurts", "Left untreated, the joint becomes more and more stiff over time"]}}, {"id": "3qsLRZVoim", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Foods to avoid to reduce gout attacks", "level": 2}}, {"id": "33hzvVPLVI", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Organ meats such as liver, kidney and brain", "Some seafood such as sardines, anchovies and shellfish", "Red meat", "Alcoholic drinks, especially beer", "Drinks high in fructose sugar"]}}, {"id": "zaZPK-xCs6", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Signs you need to see a doctor straight away", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Nw6Op0II0c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have a fever together with a very swollen, red and hot joint, see a doctor immediately, as this may be a joint infection, which must be clearly distinguished from ordinary gout."}}, {"id": "BcC82u1yf1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "l669Efn_9u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "During an acute attack, doctors usually prescribe anti-inflammatory medicine such as NSAIDs, colchicine (most effective if taken within the first 12 hours of pain) or steroids. For people with frequent attacks or persistently high uric acid, the doctor may consider medicine to lower uric acid and prevent future attacks."}}, {"id": "3ozto2TbwQ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Gout care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "4PtIBzcqD9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess and treat gout and advise on diet and medicines — no need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "gzKLnQ_TNg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "DbWkr8dgbu", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "6zEy-9J2zk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can gout be cured?
It can be well controlled with diet changes and the medicine your doctor prescribes. If you have ongoing risk factors such as genetics or other conditions, you may need long-term care."}}, {"id": "qS9Flbr9PC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is gout caused only by eating seafood?
No. Some seafood is high in purines, but other factors such as genetics, body weight and alcohol also matter a lot."}}, {"id": "RdB-tmA3Zj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How is gout pain different from osteoarthritis?
Gout usually comes on suddenly and very severely within a few hours, whereas osteoarthritis pain tends to build gradually with use. If you are not sure, let a doctor check."}}, {"id": "09wLkhNH0v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I stop my uric acid medicine on my own?
Do not stop it yourself. Always talk to your doctor first, because stopping suddenly can trigger another attack."}}, {"id": "jaUt0lXC18", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ItCmbktfgY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Gout is caused by uric acid crystals in the joints, leading to sudden, severe joint pain, usually in the big toe. Avoiding high-purine foods and alcohol, along with taking medicine as prescribed, helps control gout and prevent further attacks. If you have a fever with a very swollen, red, hot joint, see a doctor immediately."}}, {"id": "2c-oiXvGU1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "WBhm_FWYYg", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Gout: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Gout: What It Is, Symptoms & Treatment", "Arthritis Foundation – Gout: Symptoms, Diagnosis, and Treatment"]}}, {"id": "wkEY2Cvm-2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. {"time": 1788314396341, "blocks": [{"id": "MNzaDy4qdY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Severe pain in your back or side that you put down to lifting something awkwardly — but then it spreads to your lower abdomen or groin and comes in waves that keep getting worse. This may not be simple muscle pain but the classic sign of kidney stones, one of the most painful conditions people experience. This article covers the causes, symptoms and warning signs that mean you should go to hospital."}}, {"id": "liEmOtU10x", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What are kidney stones?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ezvR3G-xds", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Kidney stones are hard lumps formed when minerals and salts in the urine, such as calcium and uric acid, crystallise and stick together. They range from as small as a grain of sand to much larger. Small stones often cause no symptoms and pass out in the urine, but when a stone gets stuck in the ureter it causes severe pain."}}, {"id": "FQ4BsW-eHR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "aVSDsuIV9G", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Severe back or side pain, often in waves, spreading to the lower abdomen or groin", "Blood in the urine or cloudy urine", "Burning when passing urine, or needing to pass urine unusually often", "Nausea and vomiting"]}}, {"id": "NL7BW7zYhk", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Causes and risk factors", "level": 2}}, {"id": "fTr9c3YLFs", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Not drinking enough water, so urine is concentrated", "Eating too much salt or animal protein", "Being overweight or obese", "A family history of kidney stones", "Certain metabolic conditions that make urine minerals unusually high"]}}, {"id": "UX2rKlz07X", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: go to hospital immediately", "level": 2}}, {"id": "BSR0jUr-D7", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Pain so severe you cannot bear it", "High fever with back pain (this may mean an infection, which is much more dangerous than a simple stone)", "Constant nausea and vomiting so you cannot eat or drink", "Being unable to pass urine at all"]}}, {"id": "8F5LjhnB0r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have any of these, go to an emergency department immediately. Do not wait at home to see how it goes."}}, {"id": "c8S_N-J21C", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Self-care for small stones", "level": 2}}, {"id": "D58FnwRS0i", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If the doctor finds a small stone that is likely to pass by itself, they will usually advise you to:"}}, {"id": "tNHMwyMNFO", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Drink plenty of water to help the stone pass more easily", "Take painkillers as advised by the doctor", "Watch your symptoms and strain your urine to see whether the stone has passed"]}}, {"id": "SdYcGwDALQ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "pWVLlr11S1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most small stones pass by themselves with plenty of water and painkillers. Larger stones that cause severe pain or block the urinary tract may need to be broken up with shock waves, or removed using a scope, depending on their size and position."}}, {"id": "ptdWug485N", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Kidney stone care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "1sEBKAYzbq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess pain that may be caused by kidney stones. If there are danger signs or you need specialist treatment, we will refer you to a suitably equipped hospital straight away."}}, {"id": "kPkT-hSwSX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "VVcg0gNZCW", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "iJpXHgXc-W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does drinking lots of water really prevent kidney stones?
It helps a lot, because water dilutes the minerals in your urine so they are less likely to crystallise into stones."}}, {"id": "-k_EGzg6Me", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If I have had a kidney stone before, can I get another?
Yes, especially if you do not change your diet and drinking habits. Talk to your doctor about ways to prevent them."}}, {"id": "Vw65-OWv4r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does every kidney stone need surgery?
No. Most small stones pass by themselves. Only large stones or those blocking the urinary tract may need a procedure."}}, {"id": "8ezjqINs4b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What kind of back pain suggests kidney stones rather than muscle pain?
Stone pain usually comes in severe waves, spreads to the lower abdomen or groin, and often comes with urinary symptoms. Muscle pain tends to be a dull ache linked to posture or movement."}}, {"id": "3YuRXF1jaj", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "d8r5hw-0HG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Kidney stones form when minerals in the urine crystallise into lumps, causing severe pain when a stone gets stuck in the ureter. Most small stones pass on their own with plenty of water, but if the pain is unbearable, you have a fever, or you cannot pass urine, go to hospital immediately."}}, {"id": "1KTCAFsYWW", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "IfpKsef4Dk", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Kidney stones: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Kidney Stones: Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment", "Mayo Clinic Health System – Kidney stones: Tiny, painful, treatable"]}}, {"id": "tYGTUkaokZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If the pain is unbearable or you also have a fever, go to hospital immediately."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

They can look after themselves at home or in isolation without needing to stay in hospital."}}, {"id": "fzMZwUfW8U", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to look after yourself at home", "level": 2}}, {"id": "RPPgzdCVJ1", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Get plenty of rest and drink lots of water", "Take medicine for your symptoms as needed, such as fever reducers or cough medicine", "Check your temperature and watch your symptoms regularly", "If possible, use a separate bedroom and bathroom from others at home, and wear a mask when near other people", "Avoid sharing personal items such as cups and towels"]}}, {"id": "bawkmSQZV_", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How long should you isolate, and when can you return to normal life?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "BIBUgRzpvP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Current guidance focuses on symptoms rather than a fixed number of days. {"time": 1787651631698, "blocks": [{"id": "rVSUOf1KeG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Many people know the 3-month contraceptive injection, but not that there is also a monthly contraceptive injection — an option that works better for people whose periods became irregular on the 3-month shot. This article explains what the monthly injection is, how it differs from the 3-month shot and who it suits."}}, {"id": "T9X3RKyebQ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the monthly contraceptive injection?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "jNxBSSZz6g", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The monthly contraceptive injection is a combined hormone containing oestrogen and a progestin, unlike the 3-month injection (DMPA), which contains a progestin only. It must be given every month for continuous protection, and works by preventing ovulation like other hormonal contraceptives."}}, {"id": "4sEl54mQpQ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The main advantage over the 3-month injection", "level": 2}}, {"id": "C2GBzu6IEF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most common side effect that makes people stop the 3-month injection is irregular periods — either no periods at all or prolonged spotting. Comparative studies found that monthly injection users had clearly lower rates of irregular and prolonged bleeding than 3-month injection users", "Much less chance of periods stopping completely (amenorrhoea), compared with the 3-month injection, which often stops periods in many users", "Similar high effectiveness to the 3-month injection. If regular periods matter most and monthly visits are not a problem, the monthly injection may suit you better. If you want as few clinic visits as possible, the 3-month injection is more convenient. Yes. Talk to a doctor to plan the right time to switch."}}, {"id": "tlJKVinchf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How soon can I get pregnant after stopping?

If you are unsure whether it is right for you, talk to a doctor before deciding."}}, {"id": "lvJpKeZkRc", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "GdERWfA0bE", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["ScienceDirect – Once-a-month injectable contraceptives: efficacy and reasons for discontinuation", "CDC – U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations for Contraceptive Use, 2024"]}}, {"id": "ead2JsW5A-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. There is no serious disease, and it usually gets better within a few weeks. work"]}}, {"id": "Cx69QCiJ6y", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: see a doctor quickly", "level": 2}}, {"id": "VVCQZRm8G-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although most back But if you have danger signs — such as loss of bladder control, numbness around the buttocks, leg pain with weakness, or a fever — see a doctor immediately to find the real cause."}}, {"id": "WMPmSz5nae", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "UHvsN6Ca3a", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic Health System – 7 common low back pain FAQ", "Mayo Clinic Proceedings – Evaluation and Treatment of Low Back Pain"]}}, {"id": "vY2ViwlqgW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. vertigo-dizziness-2569.content:
{"time": 1787716044519, "blocks": [{"id": "uU356k2d-w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Suddenly the world is spinning and you cannot keep your balance. Many people panic and fear something serious. In fact, most vertigo has a harmless, treatable cause — but sometimes it is a warning sign of an emergency that needs a hospital. This article explains what causes vertigo and how to tell when it is dangerous."}}, {"id": "f7p6rKulZr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is vertigo different from ordinary dizziness?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "gBUAIQ86V3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Vertigo is the feeling that you or your surroundings are spinning when nothing is actually moving. Ordinary dizziness is more often a feeling of light-headedness, unsteadiness or poor balance, without the spinning sensation."}}, {"id": "NqdzPyYHv_", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The most common cause", "level": 2}}, {"id": "FGNHaARxUa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most common cause of vertigo is benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), which happens when tiny calcium crystals in the inner ear move out of place. It causes sudden spinning when you change your head position — looking down or up, turning over in bed or sitting up. Episodes are usually short, lasting from a few seconds to a few minutes."}}, {"id": "7m9mfy2DzD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other causes include inflammation of the balance nerve or balance organs in the inner ear, and Ménière’s disease, which often comes with a blocked feeling or ringing in the ear."}}, {"id": "PwuPfijFlM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "4AQ5NYUc_G", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["A spinning, swaying feeling or loss of balance", "Nausea and vomiting", "Symptoms that come and go, often linked to head movements (in BPPV)"]}}, {"id": "s9T02uhcQr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: go to hospital immediately", "level": 2}}, {"id": "50awUcYQUb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although most vertigo is not dangerous, it can sometimes be a sign of stroke. Remember BE FAST and go to hospital immediately if you have any of these together with dizziness or vertigo:"}}, {"id": "HEjJP4fCdT", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["B (Balance): sudden loss of balance or staggering", "E (Eyes): sudden blurred vision or loss of vision", "F (Face): drooping face — one side of the mouth droops when smiling", "A (Arms): weakness or numbness in an arm or leg on one side", "S (Speech): slurred speech, or speech others cannot understand", "T (Time): if you have any of these symptoms, go to hospital immediately — every minute counts"]}}, {"id": "cKZU1R5oVS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Also see a doctor immediately if you are confused, have trouble speaking or understanding speech, or have a sudden severe headache unlike any before."}}, {"id": "bZ-iLq1kgN", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Self-care during an episode", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ZaNuS68YhS", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Sit or lie down straight away when you feel dizzy, to lower the risk of falling", "Avoid movements that trigger symptoms", "Older adults or anyone at risk of falling should use a walking stick for support"]}}, {"id": "HQBJFan37y", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "JsDc_SP5HB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "BPPV can be treated by a doctor with specific head-positioning manoeuvres (canalith repositioning) that move the crystals back to where they do not cause symptoms. Most people improve after 1–2 sessions. Even after successful treatment, it can come back in the future."}}, {"id": "216PQJCtBg", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Vertigo checks at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "diz5Hv9o_g", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess vertigo and dizziness. If there are any of the danger signs above, we will refer you to a suitably equipped hospital straight away for your safety."}}, {"id": "I9eNOq_w_t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "b6UrBu3AiM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "fVy70epcWv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can vertigo go away on its own?
BPPV sometimes clears up by itself within a few weeks to months, but treatment by a doctor helps it clear much faster."}}, {"id": "KECdGJ6g-O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If I have had BPPV before, can it come back?
Yes. Around half of people who were successfully treated may have it again within a year."}}, {"id": "M3RlE5BTS4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which is more dangerous, ordinary dizziness or vertigo?
It does not depend on the type, but on whether you have worrying symptoms as well, such as the BE FAST signs. Those always need a hospital, whatever kind of dizziness you have."}}, {"id": "50gEd60FhY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What should older adults who often feel dizzy watch out for?
Be especially careful about falls, and see a doctor to find the cause, because older adults are more likely to have several causes at once."}}, {"id": "leSx3m40Ec", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "LKuGApsZBB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most vertigo is caused by BPPV, which is not dangerous and can be treated by a doctor with head-positioning manoeuvres. But if you have BE FAST symptoms such as a drooping face, weak limbs or slurred speech, go to hospital immediately, as these may be signs of a stroke."}}, {"id": "dhFIG5YT6P", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "l2bqFqlffP", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV): Symptoms & causes", "Mayo Clinic News Network – Recognize the sudden warning signs of stroke - and BE FAST", "CDC – Signs and Symptoms of Stroke"]}}, {"id": "6VGECz2qOi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If you have any BE FAST symptoms, go to hospital immediately."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1787720333914, "blocks": [{"id": "Q_k3uyFOWg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Suddenly your skin breaks out in raised red welts that itch all over, and you have no idea why. Hives are very common — about 1 in 5 people get them at least once in their lives. They range from small spots to large patches that join together. Hives are not contagious, and most go away on their own."}}, {"id": "1-sppRi8Nw", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common causes", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Z2uqEOlcOP", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Allergy to certain foods or medicines", "Insect bites or stings", "Very hot or cold weather, or heavy sweating", "Stress", "Tight clothing", "Some NSAID painkillers"]}}, {"id": "e1SwnewjZS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sometimes no clear cause can be found. Especially for chronic hives lasting more than 6 weeks, the doctor may need to run tests to look for a hidden cause, such as thyroid disease."}}, {"id": "FFrb3LGmvz", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How do ordinary hives differ from hives in a severe allergic reaction?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "qC7m93fNH2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This is the most important thing to know. Hives that appear suddenly can be part of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), a life-threatening emergency. Go to hospital immediately if you have hives together with:"}}, {"id": "I5Ac9_TToD", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Difficulty breathing or wheezing", "Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat", "Dizziness or feeling faint", "Severe nausea or vomiting", "Palpitations or a fast heartbeat"]}}, {"id": "KW8c_QMma5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have an adrenaline auto-injector (epinephrine autoinjector), use it immediately, and still go to hospital even if you feel better, because a severe reaction can return within a few hours."}}, {"id": "qyE_c5cGJX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ordinary chronic hives without any of the symptoms above do not carry a risk of a sudden severe allergic reaction."}}, {"id": "YGSxQYTnEo", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Self-care for ordinary hives", "level": 2}}, {"id": "KLcqul3fhg", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Avoid anything you suspect is a trigger", "Wear loose, comfortable clothing", "Avoid very hot water or long warm showers", "Take non-drowsy antihistamines as advised by a pharmacist or doctor"]}}, {"id": "cKApOIqRa7", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Gj17c_E-eh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If there are no complications or danger signs, doctors usually recommend starting with a daily non-drowsy antihistamine. If that does not work, the doctor may adjust the dose or change the medicine. For severe chronic hives that ordinary antihistamines cannot control, specialist injections may be considered under a specialist’s care."}}, {"id": "RyhJWBbqTe", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Hives care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "NoLR2qiXhs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine and treat hives. If there are signs of a severe allergic reaction, we will refer you to a suitably equipped hospital straight away."}}, {"id": "W67qhTY5qi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "KgMHmvDuwU", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "el-E6FaYeW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do hives go away on their own?
Most do. Some cases take up to 6 weeks. If they last longer, they are considered chronic hives and you should see a doctor."}}, {"id": "7q6eu2kU57", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Are hives contagious?
No. They are the body’s reaction to a trigger, not an infection."}}, {"id": "U4JIYNQ-f3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I get hives often. Should I be tested for the cause?
If they last more than 6 weeks, see a doctor to look for a hidden cause, as they are sometimes linked to other conditions such as thyroid disease."}}, {"id": "f2DSwa0WcV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Antihistamines have not cleared my hives. What should I do?
Go back to your doctor to adjust the dose or change the medicine. Do not buy more medicine on your own without advice."}}, {"id": "3ytR-YtLS5", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ohSFWW5-c4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hives are very common, and most are not dangerous and go away on their own. But if you also have difficulty breathing, swelling of the lips or throat, or feel faint, go to hospital immediately, as this may be a life-threatening severe allergic reaction."}}, {"id": "VoW4QleCYF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "ihdXasSq0l", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic Press – Hives: Causes, symptoms and relief", "Mayo Clinic – Anaphylaxis: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Hives: How To Recognize Them and When To See a Doctor"]}}, {"id": "6FRzIUjPOt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If you have hives with difficulty breathing or swollen lips, go to hospital immediately."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

allergic-rhinitis-sinusitis-2569.content:
{"time": 1787795386261, "blocks": [{"id": "Ae9NO_D2Jo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A blocked nose, runny nose and frequent sneezing — many people wonder whether it is an allergy or sinusitis, especially in Bangkok with PM2.5 dust and frequent weather changes. This article explains the differences, the symptoms to look for and how to look after yourself."}}, {"id": "Vjn1EwvQrb", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is allergic rhinitis?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "DPk_2uTWVL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Allergic rhinitis happens when the immune system overreacts to allergens in the air, such as pollen, pet hair, mould, dust mites or PM2.5 dust. The body releases histamine, which causes allergy symptoms."}}, {"id": "9zLBfX1PI1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Symptoms of allergic rhinitis", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ihTXinqC7D", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Blocked nose, frequent sneezing and runny nose", "Itchy nose, throat and eyes", "Red, watery eyes", "Headache and a feeling of pressure in the sinuses", "Dark circles under the eyes"]}}, {"id": "sAy50bYpD5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A key clue is that allergic rhinitis usually comes with itchy eyes and an itchy nose, whereas sinusitis rarely causes itching."}}, {"id": "Qb5gfyype4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is sinusitis, and how is it different?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "jhlw9oE7xf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sinusitis is inflammation and swelling of the sinuses around the nose, which stops mucus draining properly so it builds up. It often follows a common cold or poorly controlled allergies. Common symptoms are:"}}, {"id": "mXiX3D5O9E", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Blocked nose and difficulty breathing through the nose", "Thick yellow or green mucus, or mucus dripping down the back of the throat", "Pain or pressure around the eyes, cheeks, nose or forehead, especially when bending forward", "Headache, sometimes with toothache"]}}, {"id": "VYCFM2Hm6J", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to look after yourself", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ghQEIdKBwW", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Avoid allergens you suspect are triggers", "Rinse your nose with saline to clear mucus and allergens", "Use antihistamines or nasal sprays as advised by a doctor or pharmacist", "Wear a mask in areas with smoke, dust or high PM2.5"]}}, {"id": "FqEaA85VFM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ALowbFJfOh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If your symptoms get worse, do not improve with self-care, or last more than 2 weeks, see a doctor. If you have frequent or chronic sinusitis, you may need tests to find an underlying allergy and plan long-term treatment."}}, {"id": "uP7FhBnmHe", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Allergy and sinusitis care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "SiTMXF70jy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine and treat allergic rhinitis and sinusitis — no need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "YqjcaITcQ1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "ri3qmcB5Es", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "qA_GQdV_zf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can allergic rhinitis be cured?
Symptoms can usually be well controlled by avoiding triggers and using medicine, but it is not completely cured in everyone."}}, {"id": "T2-lROpRKr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does sinusitis always need antibiotics?
Not always. Most sinusitis is caused by colds or allergies, which antibiotics do not help. Let a doctor decide whether you need them."}}, {"id": "sjUv2zb237", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does PM2.5 dust really make allergies worse?
Yes. PM2.5 is one of the triggers that can worsen respiratory allergies. Wear a protective mask when dust levels are high."}}, {"id": "Ipdu46Z9Gu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How is a sinus headache different from a migraine?
A sinus headache usually comes with a blocked nose and facial pressure that gets worse when you bend forward. If you are unsure, let a doctor check."}}, {"id": "_6HgYF09r4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "O7iuN3-jrE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Allergic rhinitis and sinusitis have similar symptoms but different causes and clues. Allergic rhinitis usually causes itchy eyes and nose, while sinusitis mainly causes facial pressure and thick mucus. If your symptoms do not improve or keep coming back, see a doctor to find the cause and plan the right care."}}, {"id": "4Q9f02VtG-", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "EwZr4GYyZ5", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Cleveland Clinic – Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever): Symptoms & Treatment", "Mayo Clinic News Network – Is it allergies or a sinus infection?", "Mayo Clinic News Network – Sinusitis and treatment options"]}}, {"id": "KXsxC8t1Cd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. See a doctor if your symptoms do not improve or keep coming back."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

nhso-quota-cut-2569.title: NHSO Keeps Cutting Gold Card Benefits — Now a Weekly Quota of Just Dozens. What Does It Mean for Patients and Clinics?
nhso-quota-cut-2569.excerpt: A timeline of how Thailand’s NHSO has reduced Gold Card benefits and payments to innovative service units: from 320 to 180 baht per visit, from 2 visits a month to 2 a year, and now weekly quotas.
nhso-quota-cut-2569.seo_title: NHSO Cuts Gold Card “30 Baht Anywhere” Benefits: What Clinics Face
nhso-quota-cut-2569.seo_description: Timeline of NHSO cuts to the Gold Card “30 baht anywhere” scheme — from 320 to 180 baht per visit and new weekly quotas — and how patients and clinics are affected.
nhso-quota-cut-2569.content: {"time": 1785484443680, "blocks": [{"id": "GhEsD1DQsn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you regularly use your Gold Card (Universal Coverage) at a clinic near home, this affects you directly. Over the past year, Thailand’s National Health Security Office (NHSO) has changed the conditions for “innovative” Gold Card service units (medical clinics, pharmacies, dental clinics, Thai traditional medicine clinics and others) three times. Every change has gone in the same direction: fewer benefits, less money and more burden for both patients and service units."}}, {"id": "VhjpYd5DXM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Timeline of the actual cuts", "level": 2}}, {"id": "YDz5w0BBgn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "December 2025: the NHSO suddenly changed contract terms. Instead of paying 320 baht per visit for up to 2 visits a month, it now pays just 180 baht per visit for 2 visits a year — cutting both the payment and the number of visits at once. It also required service units to lodge a 10,000-baht guarantee and pass an audit of every medical record, with money clawed back immediately if any error was found."}}, {"id": "sb7hsM88Vw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "January 2026: the NHSO introduced a QR-code booking system that must be used within 6 hours, adding hassle for patients who have to rush to use it and for clinics that had to reorganise their queues entirely."}}, {"id": "VOyU6dPMlW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "July 2026: most recently, the NHSO changed the system again to allocate services on a weekly basis, based on data going back to March. As a result, many service units now receive a quota of only a few dozen patients a week. This means that even if your Gold Card rights are fully intact, you may arrive at a clinic and be unable to use them because that week’s quota is already full."}}, {"id": "uwD5yDA7XK", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What the NHSO says", "level": 2}}, {"id": "H3DSGCeqLj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The NHSO says the latest change aligns budget allocation with each unit’s actual services and manages the budget efficiently towards the end of the fiscal year. It stresses that Gold Card rights have not been cancelled, but that an innovative unit’s service quota for a given week may be full. It advises calling before travelling, or calling the 1330 hotline."}}, {"id": "3C8QmgDvxz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "That sounds reasonable in theory, but in practice it shifts the whole burden onto patients, who must check the quota before every visit, and onto clinics, which must hope they get enough quota for the patients who actually come. The Gold Card system was meant to make care easier to access, not harder."}}, {"id": "ldEnHWUkY9", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why this has a real impact, not just numbers on paper", "level": 2}}, {"id": "TLvA1FJ4LF", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["What happens to people who fall ill more than twice a year at an innovative service unit, when illness does not follow a quota?", "Clinics that planned their income around 320 baht per visit must suddenly adjust to just 180 baht, while the cost of medicines, supplies and staff has not fallen", "Unpredictable weekly quotas mean neither patients nor clinics can plan ahead — there may be quota today and none tomorrow", "The burden of checking rights before every visit falls on patients, especially older adults who are not comfortable with apps or phoning to ask"]}}, {"id": "pG5bPQHvDt", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "HappiWell Clinic continues to care fully for Gold Card patients", "level": 2}}, {"id": "5c7_JkvzXk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although we face the same limits as service units across the country, HappiWell Medical Clinic remains committed to caring for Gold Card patients in Thung Khru as well as the system allows. If you are worried about the quota, please message us on LINE or call before you travel, so you do not make a wasted trip."}}, {"id": "fKJg3o_Gvp", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ITgJC_6ptS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Over the past year, the NHSO has changed the conditions for innovative service units three times, each time reducing payments to service units, reducing how often patients can use their rights and making care harder to access. Although the NHSO insists rights have not been cancelled, having to check the quota before every doctor’s visit is not what a universal health coverage system should look like. We hope the NHSO will review this approach and announce changes in advance, so that patients and service units can adapt, rather than making sudden changes again and again."}}, {"id": "qyYcPM4Jog", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "k8LPjx3pju", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Hfocus – Dr Ratcharin criticises NHSO for changing innovative clinic criteria mid-stream (Thai)", "Hfocus – NHSO explains changes to Gold Card contract terms for innovative clinics (Thai)", "Hfocus – NHSO reallocates service numbers for innovative units, advises Gold Card users to call first (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "RSruESiOe5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article reflects the clinic’s views and opinions, based on publicly available news sources as of the date of publication."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

office-syndrome-2569.seo_description: What office syndrome is, why computer workers are at risk, self-care and when to see a doctor. Advice from HappiWell Medical Clinic, Thung Khru, Bangkok.
office-syndrome-2569.content:
{"time": 1786339608784, "blocks": [{"id": "iaXa4xlMOv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You sit at a computer all day, and by the end of work your neck, shoulders and upper back are stiff and aching. Many people think this is just part of office life, but these symptoms have a name — “office syndrome” — and if left untreated they can become chronic and harder to treat. This article explains what office syndrome is, what causes it and how to stop it getting worse."}}, {"id": "X_iY2XyGAB", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is office syndrome?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Qhx28PP3Ml", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Office syndrome is not a single medical diagnosis but a group of muscle and tendon pain symptoms caused by poor working posture over long periods. The main cause is usually myofascial pain syndrome, caused by tender trigger points in muscles that are used repeatedly for long periods, especially in the shoulders and neck."}}, {"id": "P7ytJOi9Pj", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "-jQtax3KkK", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Pain in the neck, shoulders, back or even knees", "Numbness or tingling in the fingers, arms or feet", "Headache and dizziness", "Tendon inflammation, such as tennis elbow from repetitive use, or wrist tendon inflammation", "Tired, sore eyes from staring at screens", "In severe cases, nausea or blurred vision"]}}, {"id": "m-NQB1Bpra", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why are office workers so often affected?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "lQun0c-IUH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Studies show that neck pain affects about 12–34% of the general population, but 50–60% of people who regularly work at computers. Sitting in the same position for long periods, bending your neck to look at screens or phones (“text neck”), and repeatedly using the same muscles without stretching all trigger painful points in the muscles."}}, {"id": "3MlVBK-Sxt", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to stop it getting worse", "level": 2}}, {"id": "qxaarFOzHk", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Get up, change position or stretch every 30–60 minutes", "Adjust your desk, chair and screen to the right height so you do not bend or tilt your neck too much", "Exercise regularly to strengthen the muscles around your neck and back", "Avoid looking down at your phone for long periods"]}}, {"id": "OAJULaJR8t", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is it treated?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "0BWXvWaCPk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If symptoms become chronic, massage may help temporarily, but without fixing your working posture the pain usually returns. Treatments doctors commonly use include trigger point injections, physiotherapy, stretching, and correcting working posture combined with exercise."}}, {"id": "gtdP4e-i89", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "JU1PxUs1Cd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have numbness or pain shooting down your arm or leg, see a doctor to rule out a trapped nerve. If the pain does not improve even after changing habits and resting, talk to a doctor to assess it and plan suitable treatment."}}, {"id": "CJnIfXfkC8", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Office syndrome care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "hPsK306Yno", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess muscle pain from office syndrome and give advice tailored to you — no need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, ideal for busy working people."}}, {"id": "T2Pkbmg4Ve", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "sPdOKe22Qa", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "u87DRdV0qc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Will massage cure it?
Massage can relieve symptoms temporarily, but without changing your working posture and habits the pain usually comes back. Fix the root cause at the same time."}}, {"id": "rt-4u2y-QB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is office syndrome linked to migraine?
Yes. Myofascial pain syndrome is linked to migraine, and people with both may need to treat them together for the best results."}}, {"id": "szo8ngHOqR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is working from home as risky as working in an office?
Just as risky, or even more so, because home set-ups often lack the ergonomic equipment an office provides."}}, {"id": "wwj0jPQUFJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which symptoms should not be ignored?
If you have numbness or pain shooting down your arm or leg, see a doctor to rule out a trapped nerve. Do not ignore it, as it can get worse."}}, {"id": "eRy4k7mmf4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "bdA4EHVnWN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Office syndrome is a group of muscle pain symptoms that are very common in people who work at computers. The main causes are poor working posture and repeatedly using the same muscles for long periods. Correcting your posture, changing position often and exercising regularly can help prevent and ease symptoms a great deal. If symptoms do not improve, or you have numbness or pain spreading down your arms or legs, see a doctor."}}, {"id": "X4kqK5ECrI", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "bxspBX5evR", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Praram 9 Hospital – Myofascial pain syndrome (Office Syndrome)", "BNH Hospital – Office syndrome: The Silent Threat for Working Adults", "MedPark Hospital – Office Syndrome: Symptoms, Causes, and Treatment"]}}, {"id": "GnAHUXywgP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. See a doctor if symptoms do not improve or you have numbness or pain spreading down your arms or legs."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

febrile-seizure-2569.excerpt: Seeing your child have a seizure with a high fever is terrifying, but most febrile seizures are harmless. What they are, how to give first aid and when to call 1669 immediately.
febrile-seizure-2569.seo_title: Febrile Seizures in Children: First Aid & When to Go to Hospital | HappiWell
febrile-seizure-2569.seo_description: Febrile seizures are frightening for parents but usually harmless. What they are, first aid steps and when to call 1669 immediately. Advice from HappiWell Medical Clinic, Bangkok.
febrile-seizure-2569.content:
{"time": 1786339924389, "blocks": [{"id": "CrPrR17Vfm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Nothing is scarier than watching your child have a seizure during a high fever, and many parents freeze. This article aims to help parents respond calmly. The good news is that most febrile seizures in children cause no lasting harm — but there are some signs that mean you must go to hospital immediately."}}, {"id": "QZ2ygLGSnR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is a febrile seizure?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "3HFIRKPpAa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A febrile seizure is a seizure caused by a high fever in a child. It is most common between 6 months and 5 years of age, with the highest risk at 12–18 months. It usually happens within the first 24 hours of a fever, and is sometimes the first sign that the child is ill."}}, {"id": "hOHqkjBGex", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does it look like?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "F11fH_afNs", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Brief loss of consciousness or not responding", "Stiffening or jerking on both sides of the body", "Eyes rolling upwards", "Possible temporary changes in skin colour or breathing"]}}, {"id": "xyPmuW8rpu", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Simple vs complex febrile seizures", "level": 2}}, {"id": "oCeHo4MuIs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Simple febrile seizures are the most common type. They last from a few seconds to about 15 minutes, do not happen again within 24 hours, and affect the whole body rather than one part."}}, {"id": "jiW8audZv7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Complex febrile seizures last longer than 15 minutes, happen more than once within 24 hours, or affect only one side of the body. These are more likely to need further assessment and care by a doctor."}}, {"id": "ZCUIsFUliw", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How dangerous are febrile seizures?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ksUOvLLKOi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This is what parents should know to ease their worries: most simple febrile seizures have no long-term effects. They do not damage the brain, do not lower intelligence, and do not mean your child has epilepsy. The risk of developing epilepsy later is only slightly higher than in other children."}}, {"id": "CJZfVMhkN5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "However, a child who has had one febrile seizure has about a 1 in 3 chance of having another, usually within the next 12 months. Children whose first febrile seizure happens before age 1 have about a 1 in 2 chance of another."}}, {"id": "YgmkKZ-PZX", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "First aid when your child has a seizure", "level": 2}}, {"id": "UTAu5bsEAe", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "ordered", "items": ["Stay calm and time the seizure from when it starts", "Lay your child on their side on a flat, safe surface, with their face turned to the side to prevent choking on saliva or vomit", "Move hard or sharp objects away from them", "Do not put anything in your child’s mouth — not fingers, spoons or cloth", "Do not hold your child down or restrain them — let the seizure run its course", "Watch your child closely until the seizure stops"]}}, {"id": "1rfrMaRmiG", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When to call 1669 immediately", "level": 2}}, {"id": "nnxLYt-dJA", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["The seizure lasts more than 5 minutes", "Another seizure follows soon after the first stops", "Difficulty breathing, or lips turning blue", "Your child does not wake up or recover well after the seizure stops"]}}, {"id": "SyABcsSSaq", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "After the seizure stops, should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "VXnKgemhRX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Always see a doctor as soon as possible after a first febrile seizure, even if it lasted only a few seconds, so the doctor can confirm it was a febrile seizure, find the cause of the fever and decide whether further tests are needed."}}, {"id": "ip7I_5tzsS", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Can it be prevented?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "u6FburX9h5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "It is still not clear why some children have febrile seizures and others do not, so there is no proven way to prevent them. For children who have had one before, the doctor may advise closer, individual fever care."}}, {"id": "I3FK2QfudJ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "See a doctor at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "LA2AJZCTVy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If your child is having a seizure that lasts more than 5 minutes or has difficulty breathing, call 1669 or go to hospital immediately — do not come to the clinic first, because your child needs a fully equipped emergency team."}}, {"id": "SOxQZpGHqE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "But if your child has had a febrile seizure and is now settled, or you would like advice on fever care to prevent another seizure, HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru is happy to help with a doctor’s consultation."}}, {"id": "J6R5mXhuWQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "qb5AJL9PkD", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "eMw_k_R9-o", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How high does a fever need to be to cause a seizure?
Febrile seizures usually happen with fevers of 38.9°C or higher, but they can also occur with lower fevers. The height of the fever does not always predict a seizure."}}, {"id": "6zQfy2J2h0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Will fever medicine prevent febrile seizures?
Fever medicine makes your child more comfortable, but it does not guarantee a seizure will not happen, because febrile seizures are linked more to how quickly body temperature changes than to the number alone."}}, {"id": "1j8CaDk_ST", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Are febrile seizures linked to vaccinations?
There is evidence of a slightly higher risk after some vaccines, such as the diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis (DTP) vaccine or the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine, because children may get a mild fever afterwards. Talk to a doctor if you are worried."}}, {"id": "Z6mfvdlcVt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Will my child develop epilepsy after a febrile seizure?
A simple febrile seizure does not mean your child has epilepsy, and the risk of epilepsy later is only slightly higher."}}, {"id": "PdXtoSUtwV", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "B6c9g-RK8V", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Febrile seizures in children are frightening for parents, but most cause no lasting harm and do not mean the child has epilepsy. The key is to stay calm, lay your child on their side to prevent choking and time the seizure. If it lasts more than 5 minutes or your child has difficulty breathing, call 1669 immediately. After the seizure stops, always see a doctor to find the cause of the fever."}}, {"id": "2XR3EddLRF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "tuXsdq94EV", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Febrile seizure: Symptoms & causes", "HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics) – Febrile Seizures in Children", "Cleveland Clinic – Febrile Seizure: What It Is, Symptoms & Treatment"]}}, {"id": "08xcBNyJMZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If your child is having a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes or has difficulty breathing, call 1669 immediately."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1786338271820, "blocks": [{"id": "dbugG97FBm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A kindergarten or nursery suddenly closing because children have hand, foot and mouth disease is something Thai parents know well, because it spreads very easily among young children. This article explains what HFMD is, which symptoms to watch for and when to take your child to a doctor quickly."}}, {"id": "UVj51xa_sR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is hand, foot and mouth disease?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "0ZwCmHLvCq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is caused by enteroviruses, most commonly coxsackievirus. However, the most common strain in East and Southeast Asia, including Thailand, is enterovirus 71 (EV-A71), which is more likely to cause severe illness than other strains. HFMD is most common in children under 5, but older children and adults can catch it too."}}, {"id": "c5Uu2oyzWM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "5x8ZvDwSf-", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Low to moderate fever", "Mouth sores, often painful enough to make eating or drinking difficult", "A rash or small blisters on the palms, soles and inside the mouth, which may spread to the knees, elbows, buttocks or genitals", "Sore throat", "Swollen glands in the neck", "Tiredness and loss of appetite"]}}, {"id": "v_ZvHkk6ut", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In babies who cannot talk yet, watch for refusing to eat or drink and unusual drooling, which may mean swallowing hurts."}}, {"id": "hX0l72H6JI", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How does it spread?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "SZe4uip_VJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "HFMD spreads very easily in several ways:"}}, {"id": "pAMpsNGWAh", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Droplets from coughing, sneezing or close conversation", "Direct contact, such as hugging, kissing or sharing cups and cutlery", "Touching contaminated toys or surfaces, then touching the eyes, nose or mouth", "The virus is also found in stools, so carers should wash their hands thoroughly after changing nappies or helping children use the toilet"]}}, {"id": "d0BWkK1gMj", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Basic care at home", "level": 2}}, {"id": "CjAGrmlQg3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "There is no vaccine and no specific treatment for HFMD, and most children recover within 7–10 days. Care focuses on easing symptoms:"}}, {"id": "_5XdpJ-wGF", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Offer water or cool drinks often to prevent dehydration, as children often do not want to drink because swallowing hurts", "Give soft, cool, easy-to-digest food and avoid spicy or crunchy food that irritates mouth sores", "Use fever and pain relief as needed", "Make sure your child gets plenty of rest"]}}, {"id": "FqXiztXcb6", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: see a doctor quickly", "level": 2}}, {"id": "oeJAVN_wD_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although complications of HFMD are uncommon, see a doctor immediately if your child has:"}}, {"id": "eEAatQo-yi", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Signs of dehydration, such as a dry mouth, clearly less urine or drowsiness", "Severe headache or a stiff neck", "Drowsiness or unusual changes in behaviour", "Abnormal breathing", "A high fever that will not come down"]}}, {"id": "I1hO_P8lmq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These may be signs of serious complications such as meningitis, which is rare but needs urgent care."}}, {"id": "DZqgnxjEU2", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How can it be prevented?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "XBPN2uIBCy", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Wash hands often — both children and carers — especially before eating and after using the toilet or changing nappies", "Regularly clean and disinfect toys, surfaces and frequently touched spots", "Avoid close contact with sick children, such as hugging, kissing or sharing items", "If your child is ill, keep them home from school until they are well, to reduce spread to other children"]}}, {"id": "vUqJII2zpU", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "HFMD care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "HYtuM8zbyb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine and treat HFMD and assess whether a hospital referral is needed if there are danger signs. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "nMmhKh5-h2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "St944jrjh_", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "LCu4CoSBFi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can a child get HFMD more than once?
Yes. It is caused by several virus strains, and having one does not protect against the others."}}, {"id": "9MFUgZ8WXr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How many days should my child stay off school?
Until the mouth sores and blisters have dried up or healed — usually about 7–10 days. Ask the doctor or your child’s teacher about when they can return."}}, {"id": "IR5MsqhuWs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can adults get hand, foot and mouth disease?
Yes, but adults usually have mild symptoms or none at all, while still being able to spread it to others."}}, {"id": "Cnoma8vUb9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is there a vaccine for HFMD?
There is currently no vaccine. The main prevention is good hygiene and avoiding close contact with people who are ill."}}, {"id": "Jzh8NohS35", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "YPb6iSHldC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hand, foot and mouth disease is common and spreads very easily among young children, especially in nurseries and kindergartens. Most cases are mild and clear up within 7–10 days, but watch for danger signs such as dehydration or neurological symptoms, and see a doctor immediately if they appear."}}, {"id": "PUVfRHuUpM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "XldiiFonog", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["CDC – About Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease", "Mayo Clinic – Hand-foot-and-mouth disease: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Hand, Foot & Mouth Disease (HFMD)"]}}, {"id": "ODizOIdkiB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. {"time": 1786338614375, "blocks": [{"id": "UcqW10oDX8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Haemorrhoids are something many people feel too embarrassed to talk about, yet they are very common — about half of adults have had them by age 50. This article explains what haemorrhoids are, how to look after yourself at home and when it is time to see a doctor."}}, {"id": "gfh6M-dayZ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What are haemorrhoids?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "pw0v9g__E0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Haemorrhoids are swollen, enlarged veins around the anus and lower rectum. Everyone naturally has this tissue; it only causes symptoms when it becomes swollen."}}, {"id": "zuCO6Lj58t", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Internal vs external haemorrhoids", "level": 2}}, {"id": "GqspTmF9Kc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Internal haemorrhoids are inside the rectum. They are usually painless and cannot be felt. The most common sign is bright red blood when passing stools. If an internal haemorrhoid pushes out through the anus (prolapse), it can become painful or bleed."}}, {"id": "wJue37FRVJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "External haemorrhoids are under the skin around the anus. These are the type that usually cause pain, itching or irritation."}}, {"id": "PnugoEUtb0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Thrombosed haemorrhoids occur when a blood clot forms in an external haemorrhoid, causing a swollen, dark purple lump and severe pain. See a doctor soon if you think you have this type."}}, {"id": "kIg8rJlSsC", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common causes", "level": 2}}, {"id": "KwcGItg8Hu", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Straining hard when passing stools", "Sitting on the toilet for too long", "Chronic constipation or diarrhoea", "Being overweight or obese", "Pregnancy", "Frequent heavy lifting or straining"]}}, {"id": "F6Z8iEmdCa", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "_Eza4MgkwX", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Itching or irritation around the anus", "Pain or discomfort, especially when sitting or passing stools", "Bright red blood when passing stools", "A swollen lump around the anus"]}}, {"id": "sDeevTxz4U", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to look after yourself at home", "level": 2}}, {"id": "d8_sbeHmry", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Eat more fibre to make stools softer and easier to pass", "Drink enough water", "Avoid straining or sitting on the toilet longer than necessary", "Use creams or suppositories for basic relief as advised by a pharmacist or doctor", "If you have chronic constipation or diarrhoea, treat that cause at the same time"]}}, {"id": "02Ej6dv3Dw", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "dQWjPuswNs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most importantly, if you have any bleeding from the anus — whether a little or a lot — always see a doctor to confirm the cause. Do not assume it is just haemorrhoids, because rectal bleeding can also be a sign of something more serious."}}, {"id": "sQmX6AOYqz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You should also see a doctor if:"}}, {"id": "-gYELPDnBZ", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Your symptoms do not improve within 1 week of self-care", "You have severe pain, especially with a swollen dark purple lump, which may be a thrombosed haemorrhoid", "Your symptoms seriously disrupt your daily life"]}}, {"id": "odX0MryDou", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Haemorrhoid treatment at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "6yxwm2jo99", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine you and advise on haemorrhoid care. There is no need to feel embarrassed or to wait until symptoms are severe. Booking is easy and private."}}, {"id": "WSg7P0GHUu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "nh1F5c9l_t", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "vQfr5JrpqC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do haemorrhoids go away on their own?
Mild symptoms sometimes improve within a few days with home care, but if they keep coming back or do not improve, talk to a doctor about long-term care."}}, {"id": "pS3jOSjkdC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need surgery?
Usually not. Most can be treated with lifestyle changes and creams or suppositories. Surgery or other procedures are usually kept for severe cases or those that do not respond to basic treatment."}}, {"id": "jo5PQ0Wzz1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Are haemorrhoids common in pregnancy?
Yes, because of the increased pressure in the abdomen. Talk to a doctor for care that is safe for both mother and baby."}}, {"id": "ubzsv8vHdx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What foods help prevent haemorrhoids?
High-fibre foods such as vegetables, fruit and whole grains, plus enough water, reduce the risk of constipation, which is one of the main causes."}}, {"id": "NYp8SHvlvX", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "VOh7nrtLOU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Haemorrhoids are very common and nothing to be too embarrassed to see a doctor about. Most can be managed with lifestyle changes and basic medicine, but if you have rectal bleeding, always see a doctor to confirm the cause rather than assuming it is just haemorrhoids."}}, {"id": "ZIHC2xp2eD", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "jdiO56_zas", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Hemorrhoids: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Hemorrhoids: Symptoms, Causes & Treatment", "Cleveland Clinic – Thrombosed Hemorrhoid: Symptoms, Causes & Treatment"]}}, {"id": "JNBsmm2q9I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If you have rectal bleeding, always see a doctor to confirm the cause."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}
