{"time": 1785483221471, "blocks": [{"id": "DKtRDUvlYR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Many people think pneumonia is just a complication of a cold, but pneumococcus — the main bacterial cause — can cause many serious illnesses, from middle ear infections to meningitis and bloodstream infection. This article looks at how well the latest pneumococcal vaccine protects you and who should especially get it."}}, {"id": "xTfUqOewVL", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How dangerous is pneumococcus?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "h07WUJSyVq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pneumococcus bacteria cause a group of illnesses called invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD), which includes pneumonia, meningitis and bloodstream infection, as well as middle ear infections and sinusitis. Worryingly, it often strikes on top of viral infections such as flu or COVID-19, making them even more severe."}}, {"id": "XNxyyVX8Zi", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who is at higher risk of severe illness?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "N0xBYw66DO", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Children under 2", "Adults aged 65 and over", "People receiving medicines or treatments that weaken immunity, such as chemotherapy or long-term steroids", "People with long-term conditions such as lymphoma, leukaemia, kidney failure, lung disease, heart disease, diabetes, or HIV"]}}, {"id": "KZi5oqoiPF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is Prevnar 20, and how is it different from earlier vaccines?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "BzHG4ON6jb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prevnar 20 (PCV20) is a conjugate vaccine covering 20 pneumococcal strains, including strain 19A, which is resistant to antibiotics — a key advantage over earlier vaccines."}}, {"id": "P6BVF7SfTC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Previously, adults wanting broad protection needed two steps: PCV13 followed by PPSV23 about a year later. It is especially recommended for:"}}, {"id": "5GShZZWvas", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["All adults aged 65 and over", "People of any age with the long-term conditions or weakened immunity listed above"]}}, {"id": "VNNUhI4G7Z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who have already had PCV13 but have not yet had PPSV23 on schedule can choose Prevnar 20 instead. Usually yes, in different arms. It also helps reduce the risk of pneumococcal complications that often follow flu. Always let a doctor assess you first."}}, {"id": "DW9YgKqwuv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I have already had PCV13. Do I still need Prevnar 20?
It depends on whether you have had PPSV23 on schedule. If not, you can choose Prevnar 20 instead. Talk to a doctor to review your vaccination history."}}, {"id": "eJhTYts-vb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need a booster after Prevnar 20?
For adults who have completed Prevnar 20 as recommended, there is currently no recommendation for a booster."}}, {"id": "8LlrUpbS3o", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I am under 65 with no long-term conditions. Can I still have it?
Yes. The vaccine is registered for adults in general, not only high-risk groups. If you want to be protected, talk to a doctor."}}, {"id": "-Lr8Xv6Q0I", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "5gOAX38USM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pneumococcus causes illnesses ranging from mild to life-threatening, especially in older adults and people with long-term conditions. Prevnar 20 offers broader protection than before with a single dose. If you are 65 or over, or have a condition that raises your risk, talk to a doctor about whether you should be vaccinated."}}, {"id": "E5VMF6HxQE", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "p3HpJN2MV8", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Bangpo Hospital – 20-strain pneumonia vaccine (Thai)", "Intrarat Hospital – IPD and pneumonia vaccine programme (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "0HK2vQp_-7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. This article gives a straightforward, no-hype look."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "wqIMz84z05", "data": {"text": "What is PRP?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "nCvUqYCwFV", "data": {"text": "PRP (platelet-rich plasma) is plasma with a higher-than-normal concentration of platelets. It is made by taking the patient’s own blood and spinning it in a centrifuge to separate out the platelet-rich part, which is then injected into the affected knee. Because it comes from the patient’s own blood, the risk of allergy or rejection is lower than with synthetic substances."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "-gely6hbQX", "data": {"text": "How much does PRP help knee osteoarthritis, according to research?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "A1PJT-NQzr", "data": {"text": "Several randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews have found that PRP is a safe and effective option for reducing pain and improving knee function in people with knee osteoarthritis. Its effectiveness is similar to hyaluronic acid injections, and it seems to work better in younger, active patients whose osteoarthritis is not yet severe."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "W4Ud-tLk4t", "data": {"text": "Pooled analyses also found that the benefits of PRP are often not obvious at first but become clearer at 6–12 months of follow-up. However, it is important to understand that the current evidence is of moderate to low quality, the improvement is partial rather than a cure, and the benefits may start to fade after about 6–9 months."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "1uVmuD2-9Y", "data": {"text": "Who is PRP for the knee suitable for?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "lRoK1KDeqb", "data": {"items": ["People with early to moderate knee osteoarthritis", "Active people who want to delay knee replacement surgery", "People who have tried painkillers or lifestyle changes without enough improvement"], "style": "unordered"}, "type": "list"}, {"id": "FuYsFYTc-Y", "data": {"text": "People with very severe knee osteoarthritis may benefit less from PRP. Always have a doctor assess whether it suits you before deciding."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "4QevkkQghj", "data": {"text": "What does the PRP knee procedure involve?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "YWioiesYqe", "data": {"items": ["Some blood is taken from the patient’s arm, just like a routine blood test", "The blood is spun in a centrifuge to separate the platelet-rich plasma", "The doctor injects the PRP back into the knee joint"], "style": "ordered"}, "type": "list"}, {"id": "6nRzxSH481", "data": {"text": "In some cases the doctor may recommend more than one injection, spaced apart, depending on the severity of symptoms and the doctor’s judgement."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "h1-UNVNV7G", "data": {"text": "Knee pain advice at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "p5nVUuS_0v", "data": {"text": "HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru does not currently offer PRP, but our doctors can assess knee pain and advise on basic care. If you would like PRP treatment, please consult an orthopaedic specialist."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "n1M-nqh-0i", "data": {"text": "For more information, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "8A7yATwDGc", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "s-IVFQqJb3", "data": {"text": "Will PRP cure my knee osteoarthritis?
It is not a cure, but it helps reduce pain and improve joint function in many patients. Results vary from person to person."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "b8DZmCFipa", "data": {"text": "Does it hurt, and how long is the recovery?
It feels similar to an ordinary joint injection. Most people do not need a long recovery, but follow the doctor’s advice afterwards."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "1ZbKKHTVu6", "data": {"text": "How many sessions are needed to see results?
It depends on the severity of symptoms and the doctor’s judgement. Some people have one injection; others may need more than one."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "77YP7GMuRP", "data": {"text": "How long do the effects last?
According to research, benefits usually become clearer at 6–12 months and may start to fade after that. But it is not a cure, and results vary. {"time": 1785923281673, "blocks": [{"id": "qGJPWjF4ua", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Knee pain when getting up from a chair, stiff joints when you wake up, or a grinding sound when you move a joint — many people think these are a normal part of getting older, but they may be signs of osteoarthritis, the most common joint disease. This article explains what osteoarthritis is, which symptoms to look out for and how to stop your joints deteriorating too quickly."}}, {"id": "28J6sCAKaV", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is osteoarthritis?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "CyjYoU0eCx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Osteoarthritis happens when the cartilage covering the ends of the bones in a joint gradually wears away, until the bones rub directly against each other. It is the most common form of arthritis and usually affects heavily used joints such as the knees, hips, hands and spine."}}, {"id": "7Md_qjnxMd", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "cG-hXjeYzk", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Joint pain, especially during or after using the joint", "Joint stiffness, most noticeable on waking or after sitting still for a long time", "Tenderness when pressing on the joint", "Reduced range of movement", "A grating feeling or grinding sound when moving the joint", "Bony lumps around the joint"]}}, {"id": "5FltVrH0bk", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How does osteoarthritis differ from rheumatoid arthritis?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "tswdnb6ipi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A helpful first clue is that osteoarthritis pain usually gets worse with use and better with rest, and morning stiffness usually eases within 30 minutes. Rheumatoid arthritis usually causes morning stiffness lasting more than an hour and often affects several joints on both sides of the body at once. However, an accurate diagnosis still needs a doctor’s examination and X-rays."}}, {"id": "yoFwR2hLkR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who is at risk of osteoarthritis?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "jIWyUmorXq", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Older age, especially over 65", "Being overweight or obese, which increases pressure on weight-bearing joints", "A previous joint injury", "Heavy, repetitive use of a joint over many years, for example from work", "A family history of osteoarthritis"]}}, {"id": "Pt53XoWv8B", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How to stop your joints deteriorating quickly", "level": 2}}, {"id": "7jIcAdtiZL", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Do low-impact exercise such as swimming, walking or cycling to strengthen the muscles around the joints", "Keep your weight in a healthy range to reduce pressure on your joints", "Avoid positions or activities that repeatedly put too much load on the joints", "For pain, paracetamol or topical pain-relief creams can help as a first step"]}}, {"id": "wR4rBMozQr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "OP9nVBRLGO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have joint pain or stiffness that does not go away, interferes with daily life or keeps coming back more often, see a doctor for an assessment and a care plan. Although osteoarthritis cannot be completely reversed, early care helps slow it down and control pain much better."}}, {"id": "K0QKxVoptu", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Osteoarthritis checks and care at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "BRGvQPIvjh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can assess joint pain and advise on care and suitable medicines — no need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "j7Ga_gVUr_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "VECxjZn49k", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "bVuRyXOoyT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can osteoarthritis be cured?
Cartilage that has worn away cannot return to normal, but pain can be controlled and further damage slowed with the right care."}}, {"id": "nD1o7qdrg3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Should I stop exercising if my joints hurt?
Do not stop completely, because not moving your joints at all can weaken the muscles around them. Choose low-impact exercise such as swimming or walking."}}, {"id": "1hKpaHZV9t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can young people get osteoarthritis?
Yes, especially people who have had a joint injury or who use their joints heavily and repeatedly, although it is more common in older adults."}}, {"id": "6Tr344OnBO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do joint supplements really help?
Results vary from person to person. Talk to a doctor before taking supplements alongside your main treatment."}}, {"id": "vUTpDMZQAh", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "UWAMS_KWG3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Osteoarthritis is the most common joint disease, caused by the cartilage in the joints wearing away with use and age. Although it cannot be completely reversed, early care — suitable exercise, weight control and seeing a doctor when you have symptoms — helps slow it down and control pain much better."}}, {"id": "ODig6Ar-8q", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "xtZM0rpl5I", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Osteoarthritis: Symptoms & causes", "Cleveland Clinic – Osteoarthritis: Symptoms, Causes & Treatment Options", "Mayo Clinic Press – Knee-pain treatment for osteoarthritis"]}}, {"id": "dialeg7yVP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. See a doctor if you have ongoing joint pain or it interferes with daily life."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

If you suspect a viral or bacterial cause, which is contagious, stay at home until your symptoms improve to reduce the spread to others."}}, {"id": "oxjiFecU3V", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I wear contact lenses while I have pink eye?

{"time": 1785554512681, "blocks": [{"id": "MurHqLxNQ_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A rushed lunch before heading straight back to your desk, a third coffee of the day, skipping meals when stressed and then eating a big meal late at night — these habits are familiar to many working people, and they are the main reasons acid reflux has become such a common health problem among office workers. This article explains what acid reflux is, how it differs from ordinary heartburn and when it is time to see a doctor."}}, {"id": "bTQodT-B_H", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is acid reflux, and how is it different from ordinary heartburn?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "2t-G12NKKf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Acid reflux happens when the muscle ring at the lower end of the oesophagus (the barrier between the stomach and the oesophagus) does not work properly, allowing stomach acid to flow back up into the oesophagus and causing a burning feeling in the chest called heartburn."}}, {"id": "OmXsf0fKZH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most people have occasional heartburn, for example after eating too much, which is normal and nothing to worry about. Many people have diabetes without knowing it, and only a small proportion of people with high blood pressure have it well controlled. Most do not find out until a health check-up or until complications have already appeared."}}, {"id": "d8NMun9Dip", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Importantly, the two often go together. Most people with diabetes also have high blood pressure, because high blood sugar over a long time can damage the blood vessels and organs involved in controlling blood pressure."}}, {"id": "eGxwWpX6AD", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who should be screened?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "CroBPtRrwB", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["People aged 45 and over should be screened for diabetes regularly", "People who are overweight (for Asians, the risk starts from a body mass index of 23, lower than the threshold used for Western populations) and have other risk factors — such as high blood pressure, a family history of diabetes or little exercise — should be screened before age 45", "All adults should have their blood pressure checked regularly, even without any symptoms"]}}, {"id": "tkhzpocBQx", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Symptoms you may notice", "level": 2}}, {"id": "UrbCtbmQl_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although they are called silent diseases, some people do have warning signs, such as:"}}, {"id": "81lYWPySKN", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Frequent thirst and frequent urination", "Blurred vision", "Unexplained weight loss", "Tiring easily"]}}, {"id": "NOhGfS6tpI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "High blood pressure usually has no warning signs at all. {"time": 1786003640895, "blocks": [{"id": "qVMuqMam_H", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Your throat hurts when you swallow, and you wonder whether it is just a cold, pharyngitis or tonsillitis — and whether you need antibiotics. This article explains the differences, the symptoms to look out for and when it is time to see a doctor."}}, {"id": "hEyyNCdMHe", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How do a cold, pharyngitis and tonsillitis differ?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Psmr2aAguM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These terms are often used interchangeably because they all involve a sore throat, but they differ in location and cause:"}}, {"id": "nJh1mzzx0G", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["The common cold is a viral infection causing a blocked or runny nose, sore throat and cough", "Pharyngitis is inflammation of the lining of the throat itself, with a sore throat as the main symptom", "Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils at the back of the throat. It is more common in children than adults, because the tonsils’ immune role decreases after puberty"]}}, {"id": "vLLQgyaLg8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "All three often occur together, and most have similar causes and basic care."}}, {"id": "G-iWeeti5T", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Most are caused by viruses and do not need antibiotics", "level": 2}}, {"id": "eOgFId6Xs_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "About 90% of sore throats are caused by viruses, such as common cold viruses or flu, which antibiotics do not help. Antibiotics should not be used unnecessarily, as this can lead to drug resistance in the long run. Symptoms usually improve within a few days with rest and symptom relief."}}, {"id": "PhOI-jnXie", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is bacterial sore throat (strep throat) different from a viral one?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "bfK5y7eOB0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only a small proportion of sore throats are caused by bacteria, most commonly group A streptococcus (“strep throat”), which needs antibiotic treatment. Left untreated, it can lead to complications such as kidney inflammation or rheumatic fever, which can cause joint inflammation, a distinctive rash or long-term heart valve damage. So do not diagnose yourself and buy antibiotics without seeing a doctor."}}, {"id": "lIGDGk-wok", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common symptoms", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ODDroj16U5", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["A sore or scratchy throat", "Pain that gets worse when swallowing or talking", "Difficulty swallowing", "Swollen, tender glands in the neck or jaw", "Red, swollen tonsils, sometimes with white spots or pus"]}}, {"id": "fY7rzZg3-P", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Basic care at home", "level": 2}}, {"id": "yopAY59UbT", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Get plenty of rest", "Drink lots of fluids", "Suck throat lozenges for relief", "Gargle with warm salt water", "Take ordinary pain and fever relief as needed"]}}, {"id": "QxXibX5Er4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "When should you see a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "Bg3C12-qiQ", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["A fever together with a sore throat", "No improvement within 24–48 hours (in children) or several days (in adults)", "Swallowing becoming harder or more painful", "Unusual tiredness", "Slight neck swelling with a worsening sore throat"]}}, {"id": "CGobzuFgbs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "See a doctor immediately if you have difficulty breathing, severe difficulty swallowing or unusual drooling, as these may be signs of a complication that needs urgent care."}}, {"id": "qQ7yhdBVMK", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Treatment for colds, sore throats and tonsillitis at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "mIHYGzrOTu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor can examine and treat sore throats, colds and tonsillitis, which are among the conditions covered by the “30 Baht Gold Card — treatment anywhere” scheme. No need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "n5m4Qwd9Hk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "GQmRNjW8KH", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "JsPoQboEb2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need antibiotics for a sore throat?
Usually not, because almost 90% of sore throats are caused by viruses. Antibiotics only work for bacterial infections. Let a doctor examine you before deciding."}}, {"id": "9gjJg2x7JP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do children get tonsillitis more often than adults?
Yes. The tonsils play a bigger immune role in childhood and less after puberty, so adults get tonsillitis less often."}}, {"id": "ieiRMcyx6B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How can I tell if it might be strep throat rather than a cold?
Strep throat usually comes on suddenly with a severe sore throat, fever and swollen neck glands, often without the blocked or runny nose of a cold. A definite diagnosis needs a doctor’s examination."}}, {"id": "yCDQfyWb6y", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can a sore throat be treated with the Gold Card?
Yes. It is one of the common illnesses that a medical clinic like HappiWell can treat under the “30 Baht Gold Card — treatment anywhere” scheme."}}, {"id": "6xRebRHe9v", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "5zy-Dw9jcG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most sore throats are caused by viruses and clear up on their own with rest and symptom relief, without antibiotics. But if you also have a fever, symptoms do not improve within a few days, or swallowing gets harder, see a doctor to check for a bacterial infection such as strep throat, because untreated it can lead to preventable complications."}}, {"id": "QJzLLJCmhi", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "u9LdBYDVlw", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Mayo Clinic – Sore throat: Symptoms & causes", "Mayo Clinic – Strep throat: Symptoms & causes", "Johns Hopkins Medicine – Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis"]}}, {"id": "t9ZEzZmLpH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. fever-comparison-2569.seo_description: How an ordinary fever, flu and dengue differ, and the danger signs that need a hospital immediately. Know when to see a doctor. HappiWell Medical Clinic, Thung Khru, Bangkok.
fever-comparison-2569.content:
{"time": 1785470860039, "blocks": [{"id": "fhgZW07C9t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When your child or you get a fever, the first thought is often “it’s just a cold — rest and it will pass”. But in the rainy season, a high fever is not always just a cold. It could be flu or dengue, and each needs different care and has different warning signs. This article helps you tell them apart and know when you really need to see a doctor."}}, {"id": "3D0_1vRvVR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does an ordinary fever look like?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "VtR1RSim4V", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A fever from a common cold virus usually comes on gradually, is not very high, and comes with a runny nose, cough and a slightly sore throat. It usually improves within 2–3 days with nothing more than rest and enough fluids."}}, {"id": "Q7oCBrDAdv", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does flu look like?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "F8dIJR3nWy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Flu comes on much more suddenly than an ordinary fever, usually with a high fever straight away, aches all over the body and exhaustion so bad you can hardly get up, along with cough, sore throat and runny nose. It differs from an ordinary fever in how severe it is and how quickly it starts. High-risk groups such as young children, older adults and people with long-term conditions may develop complications such as pneumonia. (See our flu vaccine article for more.)"}}, {"id": "xWyGJebBuz", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does dengue look like, and what do people often get wrong?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "f_DSwt4wgn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Dengue usually starts with a sudden high fever (above 39–40°C) together with at least 2 of the following: severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea and vomiting, or a rash."}}, {"id": "zZvitBoJmK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most dangerous misunderstanding is that a falling fever does not always mean you are getting better. The critical phase of dengue usually occurs around days 3–7 of the illness, often exactly when the fever starts to drop. Many people think they are recovering and stop watching for symptoms, when in fact this is the time to be most careful: about 1 in 20 people with symptoms may develop severe dengue during this phase. (See our dengue vaccine article for more.)"}}, {"id": "-Hwx1U7zbF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: go to hospital immediately", "level": 2}}, {"id": "mswwdscRDs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Whatever kind of fever you suspect, go to hospital immediately, without waiting for an appointment, if you have any of the following:"}}, {"id": "fjqdefecKG", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Severe stomach pain or tenderness", "Persistent vomiting (3 or more times in 24 hours)", "Unusual bleeding, such as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, vomiting blood or black stools", "Drowsiness, extreme tiredness, restlessness or unusually cold skin", "Rapid or difficult breathing", "A high fever for more than 2–3 days that does not come down, or a fever that has dropped but other symptoms are getting worse"]}}, {"id": "RdMe-iE8Bn", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How many days before seeing a doctor?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "1zV6ZZLHKW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If the fever is not very high and there are no danger signs, you can watch it at home for the first 1–2 days. But if a high fever lasts more than 2 days without improving, or you have symptoms that suggest flu or dengue, see a doctor for a clear diagnosis. Do not take NSAID painkillers (such as ibuprofen) on your own until dengue has been ruled out, as they may increase the risk of bleeding."}}, {"id": "noY0Xkuxh8", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "HappiWell Clinic: fever checks and quick diagnosis", "level": 2}}, {"id": "4S1SrGAOoe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have a high fever and are not sure what it is, HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru is ready to have a doctor diagnose it and advise on the right care — no need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "Rm_as0c9M6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "JACY6Qs8dx", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "uCTq1qqF-v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "My fever has gone down. Am I better?
Not necessarily — especially with dengue, where the fever dropping often coincides with the critical phase. Keep watching for other symptoms such as stomach pain, vomiting or unusual bleeding."}}, {"id": "v-uP0EEdTh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Is fever in young children different from adults?
Young children are at higher risk from both flu and dengue. Watch them especially closely and see a doctor sooner than you would for an adult if the fever does not come down within 1–2 days."}}, {"id": "etDQvTySPI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How are dengue and flu told apart?
The doctor will take a history and examine you, and in some cases do a blood test to confirm. They cannot be reliably told apart from outward symptoms alone."}}, {"id": "fEr6ekW6C8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I take fever medicine while waiting to see a doctor?
Paracetamol can be used to reduce fever according to the label, but avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or aspirin until dengue has been ruled out."}}, {"id": "Z5A5jDBkJP", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "wE2GJOTVPL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An ordinary fever, flu and dengue have different clues, but one rule applies to all: if a high fever lasts more than 2–3 days without improving, or you have danger signs such as severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding or drowsiness, see a doctor immediately. With dengue in particular, the danger often comes just as the fever starts to fall, so do not relax just because the fever has dropped."}}, {"id": "t5Dbl705Bl", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "Vfv9nICKGi", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["CDC – Severe Dengue: Know the Warning Signs", "WHO – Dengue and severe dengue", "CDC – Guidelines for Classifying Dengue"]}}, {"id": "yfOXFoe6_q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If you have a high fever or any danger signs, see a doctor immediately."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1785405088823, "blocks": [{"id": "DuD-tw14g5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "News about HIV and sexually transmitted infections often features alarming big numbers, but those numbers are often missing context and can be misleading. This article looks at verified data on the real situation, what is genuinely worrying, and how you can protect yourself."}}, {"id": "6lUnO-FVns", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "HIV in Thailand: are new infections rising or falling?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "8dH-jeT9uC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In early 2026, a widely reported figure said Thailand had about 13,000 new HIV infections. The Department of Disease Control later explained that this figure counted people newly diagnosed and registered that year, which does not mean they were all infected that year — some may have been infected years earlier but only recently tested."}}, {"id": "CxKxI9amf0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Department of Disease Control’s modelled estimates of actual new infections each year show a steady decline: from 9,230 in 2022 to 9,083 in 2023 and 8,124 in 2024. The total number of people living with HIV nationwide is estimated at around 550,000–570,000."}}, {"id": "qSKxQ1pNrM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is really worrying is not new HIV infections, but other STIs among young people", "level": 2}}, {"id": "rnZqjIVr4d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Although new HIV infections are trending down, data on other sexually transmitted infections among young people is clearly worrying. Over the past 5 years:"}}, {"id": "yE8MUuK9fU", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Syphilis among young people rose 2.7-fold, from 4,326 to 11,813 cases", "Gonorrhoea rose 2.5-fold, from 3,912 to 9,897 cases"]}}, {"id": "OmcQCrmByH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These figures show that unprotected sex is still a major problem among young people, even though awareness of prevention has grown."}}, {"id": "YQ3Nf3Iovl", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What does the example of Chiang Mai show?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "j9j9iDGpvV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Chiang Mai Provincial Public Health Office reports more than 23,900 cumulative HIV cases since surveillance began, with an average of around 700 new cases a year — about 2 a day — and young people aged 15–24 are the most worrying group. This high cumulative figure does not mean a new outbreak, but it shows that new infections continue every year, and Chiang Mai has a highly mobile population, so close surveillance is needed."}}, {"id": "b2e5_8zAb1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why do some people still not know they are infected?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "2VOuEVTOS_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A key problem public health experts always stress is that many people live without knowing their infection status, because there are no clear symptoms early on, so they may pass it on without realising. The good news is that with early diagnosis and continuous antiretroviral treatment, the virus can be suppressed to undetectable levels, which means it is not passed on to others, and people can live completely normal lives."}}, {"id": "iXJ-bRF9Gh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Thai citizens can currently get a free HIV test twice a year at a nearby health facility, or get a self-test kit through the Pao Tang app (Health Wallet menu > preventive health benefits), with preliminary results in 20 minutes."}}, {"id": "R29dHModVg", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Condoms protect more than you might think", "level": 2}}, {"id": "P8roQlj4hR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Of all prevention methods, condoms are the only one that protects against both HIV and other sexually transmitted infections at the same time, such as syphilis, gonorrhoea and HPV. PrEP, by contrast, protects only against HIV. So condoms are still recommended every time you have sex, even if you are using another method of protection."}}, {"id": "3tCD1inv_g", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you have recently been at risk of HIV exposure, or are interested in preventive medicine, read more about PEP and PrEP in our article on the difference between PEP and PrEP."}}, {"id": "x3nGFwFDlM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Free condoms in all sizes at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}}, {"id": "FCoZ_gmKAU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru gives out condoms free of charge in all sizes. Just drop by the clinic — there is no cost — and feel free to talk to a doctor about sexual health. No need to feel embarrassed or wait for symptoms before coming in. Prevention is always better than cure."}}, {"id": "kW6WQlX0Ad", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For more information, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "Pai8U0HCOg", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "x1JBkTvkZY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I have only one partner. Do I still need protection?
Yes. Risk can come from your own or your partner’s past, if your partner has never been tested. Testing and protection do not mean you do not trust each other — they are a way of looking after your health together."}}, {"id": "XnporwTBUC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does an HIV test hurt, and how soon do I get the result?
It is a blood test or a self-test kit, with preliminary results in about 20 minutes."}}, {"id": "OHxI7DFmLp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I have no symptoms at all. Do I need to be tested?
Yes. HIV and many other STIs often cause no clear symptoms early on. Testing is the only way to know your real status."}}, {"id": "P5xg0laoYG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I have to buy anything else to get free condoms at the clinic?
No. Just drop by and pick them up — no conditions."}}, {"id": "pK_UXHjitA", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "uLa58aIMnK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "According to the Department of Disease Control, new HIV infections in Thailand are trending down. What is still genuinely worrying is the clear rise in other sexually transmitted infections among young people, and the many people who do not know their status. Regular testing and using a condom every time remain the most effective protection. Pick up free condoms at HappiWell Clinic at no cost."}}, {"id": "a4Ntau3LWk", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "kbtL2hsOco", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Thai PBS PolicyWatch – Gen-Z HIV infections rising: is the epidemic coming back? (Thai)", "Thai PBS – Chiang Mai monitors HIV, gives treatment within 24 hours of diagnosis (Thai)", "Thai Health Promotion Foundation – Ministry of Public Health releases Thai HIV statistics (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "O38v1eaHHb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1785468272026, "blocks": [{"id": "oeiehRaCh8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every time you walk into a pharmacy or clinic, there are so many contraceptive options that it is hard to choose: pills, injections, IUDs, implants and condoms. Each has its pros and cons. No method is “the best” for everyone — only the one that best fits your lifestyle and body."}}, {"id": "ENbTGkKBc4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article compares widely used contraceptive methods, how effective they really are and who they suit, and answers a common question: can you get contraception for free?"}}, {"id": "0jRuBQOhoV", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why choose what suits you, not just what a friend recommends?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "4zJY47GECA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each method works differently. Some rely on you being consistent, such as taking a pill at the same time every day; others are given once and last for months or years without you having to think about them. This makes a big difference to how effective each method is in real life, even though some are almost 100% effective in theory."}}, {"id": "cVzaH3dwbs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choosing a method that does not suit you — such as the pill when you often forget to take tablets — is a leading cause of preventable unplanned pregnancies."}}, {"id": "K3Njxtwjpc", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Comparing popular contraceptive methods", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ZFb1uDX5Iq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The contraceptive pill
Must be taken at the same time every day. Used perfectly, it is very effective, but in real life, where people sometimes forget, about 7% of users have an unplanned pregnancy each year. It suits people who are confident they will not forget, and who also want to regulate their periods or reduce acne."}}, {"id": "wrHEIwEso3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The 3-month contraceptive injection (DMPA)
One injection gives 3 months of contraception, with no daily pill to remember. In real-life use, about 4% of users have an unplanned pregnancy. It suits people with busy lives who forget easily or find daily pills inconvenient. Good to know: periods may become irregular or stop while using it, and after stopping it may take some time before fertility returns to normal."}}, {"id": "LeumX7go7o", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Intrauterine devices (IUDs) and contraceptive implants
The most effective of all reversible methods, with an unplanned pregnancy rate below 1%, because they do not depend on the user at all. Inserted once, they last from 3 to 10 years depending on the type. They suit people who want long-term contraception without frequent attention."}}, {"id": "-xCw6ldLta", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Condoms
Less effective in real-life use than hormonal methods and IUDs (up to about 13–18% unplanned pregnancies a year if not used consistently), but they are the only method here that also protects against sexually transmitted infections, so they are often recommended together with another method for double protection."}}, {"id": "MalaHDhgvh", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who is the 3-month contraceptive injection especially suitable for?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "PkBqMywf2B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Of all the options, the 3-month injection is very popular with working people because:"}}, {"id": "SGtapmvH0z", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["You do not have to think about it every day like the pill — just remember your next injection date", "It suits people who had side effects from combined hormonal pills (oestrogen + progestin), because the injection contains a progestin only", "It reduces menstrual bleeding in many people, so it suits those with heavy periods"]}}, {"id": "ECt8P4K41W", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One thing to consider: if you plan to have a baby soon, it may not be your first choice, because ovulation can take several months to return after stopping. Talk to a doctor to plan ahead."}}, {"id": "u1gKt3-P1y", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Can you get contraception for free? What does the Gold Card cover?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "aEAmpEGNJt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Thailand’s National Health Security Office (NHSO) provides free contraception for people of reproductive age under the 30 Baht Gold Card, covering the pill, injections, implants, IUDs and emergency contraception to prevent unplanned pregnancy. Ask about using your rights at the service unit near home where you are registered."}}, {"id": "XMoDDdDxuF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Where to get the 3-month injection, and how much does it cost?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "clEInNUtbR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prices for the 3-month contraceptive injection (DMPA) vary between clinics, depending on the location and whether a consultation is included."}}, {"id": "SneqC-x1Zl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, the 3-month contraceptive injection costs 100 baht, with a doctor’s consultation before every injection to check it suits your body and health history. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "S7z265K1by", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book your contraceptive injection, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "QZ9IIddqM4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "UBO0K_8X_p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does the 3-month injection really cause weight gain?
It is a side effect in some people, and how much varies from person to person. Talk to a doctor if you are concerned."}}, {"id": "P04ZrjSaG-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need to wait for my period before my first injection?
Doctors usually recommend having it early in your cycle to be sure you are not already pregnant. Talk to a doctor to plan the right day."}}, {"id": "I9DV9Y7gaW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I get pregnant straight after stopping?
Everyone’s body responds differently. Some people ovulate again quickly; for others it may take several months. If you are planning a pregnancy, talk to a doctor in advance."}}, {"id": "5eec2BZ_wR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does the contraceptive injection protect against STIs?
No. It only prevents pregnancy. To protect against sexually transmitted infections as well, use condoms too."}}, {"id": "CWkDUXVNqq", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "HtpqoF-iql", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "No contraceptive method is “the best” for everyone. Each has pros and cons depending on your lifestyle and health. The 3-month injection is a convenient choice for people who do not want to worry about remembering a daily pill. If you are not sure which method suits you, talk to a doctor to assess your health and goals before deciding."}}, {"id": "9uRDC6RUTr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "YL0ygHEtTI", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["CDC – U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations for Contraceptive Use, 2024", "Guttmacher Institute – Contraceptive Effectiveness in the United States", "Government Public Relations Department – Free contraception for people of reproductive age under the Gold Card (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "b0hjJLsed0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. Always talk to a doctor before choosing a contraceptive method."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

{"time": 1785403948247, "blocks": [{"id": "NCHOVKZwFj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Many people use “flu” and “a cold” as if they mean the same thing, but their severity is very different. Most colds clear up on their own in 2–3 days, but flu causes a sudden high fever, aches all over and severe exhaustion, and in some people it develops into pneumonia that needs a hospital stay."}}, {"id": "NSVQtmZae6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This year, Thailand’s Department of Disease Control warned early on that flu in 2026 is likely to be worse than last year. This article looks at the current situation, what the vaccine can do, who should especially get it and where to get vaccinated."}}, {"id": "g-afm1wbi5", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How is flu different from a cold, and why is it more dangerous?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "mxe5qMGnq8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Flu is caused by the influenza virus, which spreads faster than common cold viruses, causes more severe symptoms and comes on suddenly. People usually get a high fever straight away, aches throughout the body, cough, sore throat, runny nose and exhaustion so bad they can hardly get up. Cold symptoms, by contrast, come on gradually and are milder."}}, {"id": "YMt1KY4-jK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In high-risk groups — young children, older adults, pregnant women and people with long-term conditions such as lung disease, heart disease, diabetes or weakened immunity — flu can lead to serious complications such as pneumonia, a leading cause of hospital admissions and deaths each year."}}, {"id": "IowlFoM1Z4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The flu situation in Thailand in 2026", "level": 2}}, {"id": "l27PsJ7UZ-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In March 2026, the Department of Disease Control, Ministry of Public Health, warned that flu cases this year were likely to be higher than last year as social activities and travel picked up again. According to the latest digital disease surveillance data at the end of May 2026, there had already been more than 171,731 cases and 16 deaths. Although the numbers had started to fall from the beginning of the year, they were still above the 5-year median."}}, {"id": "qa4KtJqlU6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The age group with the highest rate of illness is children aged 5–9, followed by young children aged 0–4 and 10–14. The most commonly detected virus this year is influenza B. In 2025, Thailand reported 1,194,342 flu cases and 129 deaths for the whole year — a reminder that this is not a disease to ignore."}}, {"id": "XNJAeInrcg", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the flu vaccine, and how well does it protect you?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "eji9wToAqw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The flu vaccine used in Thailand is quadrivalent (4-strain), covering two influenza A strains and two influenza B strains. Its make-up is updated every year following World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations, to best match the strains expected to circulate that season."}}, {"id": "o5B-woSvY0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How effective the flu vaccine is varies from year to year, depending on how well the circulating strains match the forecast. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in the 2025–2026 season the vaccine reduced the risk of illness from influenza A by about 30–34% and from influenza B by as much as 45–71% — good news this year, since influenza B is the main strain circulating in Thailand right now. Although effectiveness is not 100%, the CDC confirms that the vaccine still significantly reduces the severity of illness and the chance of needing a hospital stay."}}, {"id": "SzX2YhMGBK", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who should especially get the flu vaccine?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "oDOV3ErFpF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The CDC recommends that everyone aged 6 months and over gets a flu vaccine every year, but the groups that should give it particular priority because they are at risk of severe illness are:"}}, {"id": "lMAkIPkTke", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Young children under 5, and especially children aged 5–9, who have the highest rate of illness this year", "Adults aged 65 and over", "Pregnant women", "People with long-term conditions such as chronic lung disease, heart disease, diabetes or weakened immunity", "Healthcare workers and people who care closely for high-risk groups"]}}, {"id": "439hLCRo6v", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How many doses, and how often?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "1lsfAfM0u8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Adults and children aged 9 and over need just one dose a year. Children under 9 having their first flu vaccine may need 2 doses at least 4 weeks apart, as advised by the doctor. Because protection fades over time and the circulating strains change every year, a yearly vaccine is recommended — it is not a one-off."}}, {"id": "3vfZdJkPT1", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Where to get the flu vaccine, and how much does it cost?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "jzmGze-cMe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru offers the quadrivalent flu vaccine for 390 baht per dose, with a doctor taking your history and assessing you before every injection. No need to travel to a big hospital. Booking is easy, with no long wait."}}, {"id": "sWtmNe82pu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book your flu vaccine, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "VDEvZ1U6tB", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "rzqQUqNQo8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I still get flu after being vaccinated?
Yes, because the vaccine is not 100% protective, but it greatly reduces your chance of getting ill and the severity of symptoms, especially the chance of needing a hospital stay."}}, {"id": "zD62UydZ4P", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I have the flu vaccine and a COVID vaccine at the same time?
Usually yes, but always let a doctor assess you based on your health and history first."}}, {"id": "dyoS6-JA6l", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I am pregnant. Can I have the flu vaccine?
Yes, in any trimester, and pregnant women are especially recommended to have it, because pregnancy increases the risk of severe illness from flu."}}, {"id": "9mfx1OGHaf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How many times a year, and do I really need it every year?
Once a year for adults and children aged 9 and over, and yes, every year, because the circulating strains change and protection from the vaccine fades over time."}}, {"id": "bNovTZRH8Q", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "m9Ac0sHIcj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "As the Department of Disease Control has warned, flu in 2026 is likely to be worse than last year, especially among young children, who have the highest rate of illness. The quadrivalent flu vaccine significantly reduces the risk of illness and the severity of symptoms, especially this year, when influenza B — which the vaccine protects against well — is the main strain. If you are in a high-risk group or simply want to protect yourself, talk to a doctor and get vaccinated today."}}, {"id": "aiy6vTE_Jc", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "h4CMuZ9MUE", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["CDC – Seasonal Flu Vaccine Basics", "CDC – Interim Estimates of 2025–26 Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness", "Hfocus – Warning: flu in 2026 may rise above last year (Thai)", "Onlinenewstime – Rainy-season flu 2026: 170,000 cumulative cases (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "eMIgPOktYI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. Always talk to a doctor before deciding on any vaccination."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

pep-prep-2569.content:
{"time": 1785402471773, "blocks": [{"id": "9v6M4mmizN", "data": {"text": "Many people have heard of PEP and PrEP but are confused about how they differ, when to take them, and whether it is still in time if they have just had a risk."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "0Ev7PADdqO", "data": {"text": "The key thing to know before reading on: if you have just had a possible HIV exposure, get PEP as soon as possible. Do not wait or hesitate, because this medicine really does have a limited time window."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "MkJoHbJzpy", "data": {"text": "What are PEP and PrEP, and how do they differ?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "ykqcVhZZC4", "data": {"text": "Both are antiretroviral medicines from the same group used to treat HIV, but they are used in different situations:"}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "5hEswAsTKL", "data": {"items": ["PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis) is medicine taken “before a risk”, regularly and in advance, by people at ongoing risk — for example those with several partners, a partner whose HIV status is unknown, or a partner living with HIV", "PEP (post-exposure prophylaxis) is “emergency medicine after a risk”, used when there has just been a possible exposure — for example a condom breaking, sex without protection, or accidental contact with someone else’s blood or body fluids"], "style": "unordered"}, "type": "list"}, {"id": "-qIRqm99t8", "data": {"text": "The key difference is that PrEP must be taken consistently in advance to work, while PEP must be started as soon as possible after the event."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "IQb2Q_W363", "data": {"text": "How urgent is PEP, and what does it involve?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "LRJPlOFM-E", "data": {"text": "Public health organisations worldwide and in Thailand agree that PEP must be started as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure. The sooner you start, the better the chance of preventing infection. Once this window has passed, the medicine no longer works."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "Q9qzr0x9ZH", "data": {"text": "Before starting PEP, the doctor will do a blood test to check whether you already have HIV (if you do, this regimen cannot be used), as well as tests for hepatitis B and liver and kidney function. You then take the medicine every day for the full 28 days, with repeat blood tests at 1 month and 3 months after finishing to confirm the result. Until you have finished the course, do not donate blood, and use a condom every time you have sex."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "m7KbvIXpcC", "data": {"text": "Who is PrEP for, and how effective is it?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "U18PovBg85", "data": {"text": "PrEP is a combination of 2 medicines taken as one tablet a day, consistently. Research shows that when taken as recommended, it reduces the risk of getting HIV from sex by about 90% or more, and from sharing needles by more than 70%. But its effectiveness drops a lot if it is not taken consistently."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "K90p3d0ply", "data": {"text": "Before starting PrEP, you must have an HIV test to make sure you are not already infected, because this medicine is only for people who do not have the virus. Also note that PrEP only protects against HIV, not other sexually transmitted infections such as gonorrhoea, syphilis or HPV, so condoms are still recommended for broader protection."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "tpKYfIFB2c", "data": {"text": "Can you get PrEP or PEP for free?", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "WjmlCx4HLq", "data": {"text": "Some service units under the Gold Card provide free PrEP for people at risk, such as the Thai Red Cross AIDS Research Centre (Anonymous Clinic) and other participating units. Contact those units directly for more information."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "T6t4TjFimM", "data": {"text": "PEP/PrEP at HappiWell Clinic", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "2y3Uo46lDM", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor provides risk assessment, blood tests and PEP/PrEP medicine."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "3I8z7KwTRr", "data": {"text": "Please book on LINE before every visit. If you have just had a possible exposure and need PEP, message us on LINE straight away — the sooner the better, because PEP has the limited time window explained above."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "EuAOMDe8gq", "data": {"text": "For service and medicine prices, please ask us on LINE."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "OHU67z6NRx", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "OzmrMoN6ny", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "oZ53IwJoVK", "data": {"text": "It has been more than 72 hours. Can I still get PEP?
Its effectiveness drops sharply after this window. See a doctor as soon as you can, however many hours have passed, so you can assess the situation together."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "TpybxvGpVA", "data": {"text": "I am already taking PrEP. Do I still need condoms?
Using both is still recommended, because PrEP only protects against HIV, not other sexually transmitted infections."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "VzSHDUDcj7", "data": {"text": "If I forget PrEP on some days, am I still protected?
Protection decreases with less consistent use. If you often forget, talk to a doctor to reassess your risk."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "MBT-SidQrL", "data": {"text": "Does the HIV test before starting medicine hurt, and how long does it take?
It is an ordinary blood test and does not take long. The doctor will always explain the steps and how long results take before you start."}, "type": "paragraph"}, {"id": "dl2OxzuSkQ", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}, "type": "header"}, {"id": "7N3T3UiAeJ", "data": {"text": "PrEP is preventive medicine taken in advance by people at ongoing risk, while PEP is emergency medicine that must be started as soon as possible, within 72 hours of exposure. {"time": 1785475618189, "blocks": [{"id": "6ZJMLO2EpQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Many people know about flu and pneumococcal vaccines but are less familiar with the RSV vaccine, even though RSV is as important a cause of severe respiratory illness in older adults as flu. This article explains what RSV is, how well the vaccine protects you and who should especially get it."}}, {"id": "Ga2MAM18Gd", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is RSV, and how dangerous is it?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "OPWirp-e3k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) causes respiratory infections. In healthy people it usually causes cold-like symptoms — runny nose, cough and sore throat — and clears up on its own. But in high-risk groups such as older adults, people with chronic lung or heart disease and babies, it can spread to the lungs and cause severe bronchiolitis or pneumonia that needs hospital treatment."}}, {"id": "Rukb29nd8r", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who is at risk of severe RSV illness?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "HS2mHcJS00", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Adults aged 60 and over", "People with chronic lung disease, heart disease or weakened immunity", "Babies and young children, who can be protected indirectly by vaccinating the mother during pregnancy"]}}, {"id": "UD8SaPlZGF", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the RSV vaccine, and how well does it work?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "MI-jHU664m", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The vaccine currently used is Abrysvo, which covers both RSV subtypes A and B. In a study of more than 34,000 adults aged 60 and over, the vaccine reduced the risk of RSV lower respiratory tract disease by 67% compared with those who were not vaccinated."}}, {"id": "Iy0yGsZ3Xm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "As well as older adults, Abrysvo is approved for pregnant women at 24–36 weeks, passing immunity on to protect the newborn up to 6 months of age — the period when babies are most at risk of severe RSV."}}, {"id": "5sWg60HkFL", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who should get it, and how many doses?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "KTVLz0Tz4X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The RSV vaccine is a single dose — it does not need to be repeated every year like the flu vaccine. It is recommended for:"}}, {"id": "oCtDMcdGP5", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["All adults aged 60 and over", "Adults aged 50–59 at high risk of severe illness, such as those with lung disease, heart disease or other long-term conditions — talk to a doctor to assess suitability", "Pregnant women at 24–36 weeks, to protect the newborn"]}}, {"id": "vPRS6trhMH", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Where to get the RSV vaccine, and how much does it cost?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "zj_j7h_9C7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prices for the RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) vary between clinics and private hospitals in Bangkok."}}, {"id": "FvLQ666GZR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, the RSV vaccine costs 7,200 baht per dose, with a doctor’s consultation before every injection to check it suits your health."}}, {"id": "VPoI22ywdk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book your RSV vaccine, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "1jFr6WjVYc", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "mpVfCi_OQP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Do I need an RSV booster every year?
Currently only one dose is recommended. There is not yet clear data on if or when a booster is needed, and doctors will follow updated recommendations."}}, {"id": "dP-ggDm1wC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Can I have the RSV vaccine at the same time as the flu vaccine?
Usually yes, in different arms, but always let a doctor assess you based on your health first."}}, {"id": "Ss1WP-lQ5n", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I am under 50. Can I have it?
Current recommendations focus on people aged 50 and over, or pregnant women within the recommended weeks of pregnancy. Younger people should talk to a doctor if they have specific risks."}}, {"id": "XWZCLQbFg9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I am pregnant. Is the RSV vaccine safe?
The vaccine is approved for pregnant women at 24–36 weeks to protect the newborn. Talk to a doctor to plan the right timing."}}, {"id": "bLPqYe0YdR", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "0q-Ec3ZWBj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "RSV is a more dangerous respiratory virus than many people think, especially for older adults and people with long-term conditions. The Abrysvo vaccine significantly reduces the risk of severe lower respiratory tract disease with just one dose, not a yearly shot. If you are 50 or over, or pregnant, talk to a doctor about whether you should be vaccinated."}}, {"id": "kYpUBRG3Dt", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "z43BT5L4Dh", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["European Medicines Agency – Abrysvo", "CDC – Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule"]}}, {"id": "SWl2a0ApxS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. Always talk to a doctor before deciding on any vaccination."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}

rabies-vaccine-2569.content:
{"time": 1785404248875, "blocks": [{"id": "kXKvkMc9yl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Many people think a small bite or scratch from a dog or cat is nothing to worry about — just rinse it and leave it. But the disease that can come with a bite or scratch is far more frightening than you might think, because once rabies symptoms begin, almost no one survives."}}, {"id": "rRGW1j_1g6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The good news is that rabies is almost 100% preventable if you take the right steps from the start. This article explains what to do immediately after a bite, whether you need a vaccine, the current situation in Thailand and where to get care."}}, {"id": "jdl8vyAG3S", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How dangerous is rabies, and why can’t you take chances?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "gVXYdmQP-G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rabies is a viral infection that enters the body through a wound, usually from an infected animal’s saliva when it bites or scratches. The virus travels along the nerves to the brain, which is why there is no cure once symptoms begin. Almost everyone who develops symptoms eventually dies."}}, {"id": "eDtXtdWnoU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most dangerous thing is that many people think a small wound is nothing, or do not want to spend time going to hospital, so they never get the preventive vaccine. In reality, the incubation period can last weeks to months, which means there is still time to prevent rabies if you get vaccinated on the day you are bitten — do not wait for symptoms, because by then the vaccine can no longer help."}}, {"id": "TdsPURmD5K", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The rabies situation in Thailand in 2026", "level": 2}}, {"id": "EBuGYuHR-P", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Department of Disease Control, Ministry of Public Health, reported that over the past month (data as of 10 July 2026), rabies caused the most deaths of all monitored diseases, with 7 deaths so far this year and more than 21,633 people receiving post-exposure vaccination, a number that is rising compared with the previous month."}}, {"id": "v1mNLibat_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Department of Disease Control’s analysis shows that about 9 in 10 infections come from dog bites and the rest from cats, and the main reason almost everyone who died did so was that they “did not see a doctor for a vaccine after being bitten or scratched”, thinking the wound was too small to matter. The Department always stresses: “Rabies is fatal in every case once symptoms appear, but it is preventable.”"}}, {"id": "-ti_NunhIb", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Bitten, scratched or licked on a wound: what to do first", "level": 2}}, {"id": "o09yXFCi_E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The World Health Organization (WHO) advises that, however small the wound, you should do the following immediately:"}}, {"id": "bI_Iob9goB", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "ordered", "items": ["Wash the wound with clean water and soap immediately for at least 15 minutes to reduce the amount of virus in the wound — one of the most effective steps in preventing rabies", "Apply an antiseptic, such as povidone-iodine (Betadine), after washing", "Watch the animal that bit you. If possible, observe it for 10 days (for an owned pet). If it is a stray or its history is unknown, treat it as a risk and see a doctor immediately without waiting", "See a doctor quickly to assess the wound and decide on vaccination — do not wait for the wound to heal first"]}}, {"id": "mKHZkIptxY", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Which wounds need a vaccine, and which need an extra injection?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "RMtSo1Q-kk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The WHO divides wounds into 3 risk levels to decide on the right treatment:"}}, {"id": "kAFCxGCkWe", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Low risk: touching or being licked on unbroken skin. The risk is very low and a vaccine is usually not needed, but have a doctor assess it to be sure", "Moderate risk: a superficial bite or scratch without bleeding. You need the preventive vaccine immediately", "High risk: a deep bite that bleeds, multiple bites, wounds on the face, head, neck or hands, or animal saliva in contact with the eyes, mouth or nose. As well as the vaccine, you need rabies immunoglobulin injected around the wound to give immediate protection while the vaccine takes effect — a step that must be done at a hospital specially equipped for it"]}}, {"id": "3RN0V8tmgJ", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How many doses of rabies vaccine, and how far apart?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "fuJWvIOVCM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For people who have never had a rabies vaccine, the doctor will follow the standard schedule on days 0, 3, 7 and 14 after the bite (in some cases the doctor may add a booster on day 28, depending on the wound risk and the doctor’s judgement). People who were vaccinated in advance usually need only 2 booster doses. The key is to complete every dose on schedule and never stop partway, even if the wound seems to have healed."}}, {"id": "jwhtmgq4IV", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "The “5 don’ts” to reduce the risk of being bitten", "level": 2}}, {"id": "u8fINVjd1X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "As well as knowing what to do after a bite, preventing bites in the first place is just as important. The Department of Disease Control recommends these “5 don’ts”:"}}, {"id": "i-ftZfy_E5", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Don’t tease animals or make them angry or frightened", "Don’t step on an animal’s tail, head, body or legs", "Don’t separate fighting animals with your bare hands", "Don’t take away a food bowl or move food while an animal is eating", "Don’t approach animals you do not know or whose history is unknown"]}}, {"id": "gtbw7pmR4S", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "And if you keep a dog or cat at home, remember to have it vaccinated against rabies every year, because fully vaccinated pets are an important shield for both the animal and the people at home."}}, {"id": "uWtvrFcWNS", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Bitten — where should you go, and how much does it cost?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "0xei1myGW1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, a doctor cleans the wound, assesses the risk and gives the rabies vaccine as soon as you arrive, with no long wait. Prices are:"}}, {"id": "BC59QSQXu1", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Rabies vaccine: 390 baht per dose", "Wound cleaning/dressing: 50 baht", "Stitches (if needed): 50 baht per stitch"]}}, {"id": "m13vCcQv3_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For severe wounds — such as deep bites, heavy bleeding, multiple bites, or wounds on the face, head, neck or hands — that also need rabies immunoglobulin, the clinic will refer you straight away to a suitably equipped hospital for your safety, without unnecessary waiting or risk."}}, {"id": "zDPwHTrOQb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. We are open every day: Monday–Friday 08:00–18:00 and Saturday–Sunday 08:00–12:00."}}, {"id": "OgXgR-lD-F", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Frequently asked questions", "level": 2}}, {"id": "YKRHrYb13q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The bite is very small and not bleeding. Do I need the vaccine?
Always let a doctor assess it first, because the risk depends on several factors such as the type of animal, where the wound is and the animal’s history. Do not decide for yourself that it is nothing."}}, {"id": "ceKIoJSd0D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The animal that bit me seems normal. Do I still need the vaccine?
If it is an owned pet that can be observed for 10 days, the doctor may decide case by case. But if it is a stray or its history is unknown, getting vaccinated is always recommended, because the virus can be passed on before the animal shows symptoms."}}, {"id": "mm-GVfQdyk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Does the vaccine hurt a lot?
It feels like any ordinary vaccine. Possible side effects are slight pain, swelling and redness at the injection site, which go away on their own."}}, {"id": "KoHEVRdV6f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "I am pregnant. Can I have the rabies vaccine?
Yes, because rabies is fatal for both mother and baby if not prevented. The doctor will give the vaccine as appropriate."}}, {"id": "1ACjfF9OTD", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Summary", "level": 2}}, {"id": "pitng6Wzhd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rabies is almost 100% preventable but untreatable once symptoms begin. The key is “wash the wound immediately, see a doctor quickly and complete every vaccine dose”, however small the wound looks. If you or someone close to you is bitten, scratched or licked on a wound by a dog, cat or other mammal, do not wait to see what happens — get assessed by a doctor as soon as possible."}}, {"id": "N8xQS3bvK4", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "References", "level": 3}}, {"id": "WDKZxVn9S4", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["World Health Organization – Rabies vaccinations and immunization", "CDC – Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis", "Hfocus – Top 5 illnesses and causes of death, June–July 2026 (rabies caused the most deaths) (Thai)", "Department of Livestock Development – The “5 don’ts” to prevent rabies (Thai)"]}}, {"id": "W1QBhBK_q7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This article is for general information and is not personal medical advice. If you are bitten or scratched by an animal, see a doctor immediately without waiting."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}
