dengue-vaccine-2569.content:
{"time": 1785405661344, "blocks": [{"id": "esixE-QBtF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every rainy season, besides clothes taking longer to dry, one thing arrives without fail: dengue. Many people think of it as a children’s disease, but adults can become seriously ill too — and, more worryingly, if you have had it once, a second infection can be many times more severe."}}, {"id": "2XjzLdXh5r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More and more people are asking about the dengue vaccine. This article looks at how serious dengue is, the situation this year, whether the vaccine really works and what to know if you plan to get it."}}, {"id": "LE0NlsJqr0", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "How dangerous is dengue really?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "dAUwp9_tMu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, which has 4 types (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and is spread mainly by Aedes mosquitoes that bite during the day. Unlike a common cold, dengue has no specific cure. Doctors can only support the patient and watch for complications such as abnormal bleeding or shock from plasma leakage, which can be life-threatening if the patient reaches hospital too late."}}, {"id": "lBPjAeWFa0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What makes dengue different from most infections is “reinfection”. After being infected with one type, the immune system remembers that type, but if you are later infected with another type, the body may react abnormally and the illness can be more severe than the first time. This is why people who have had dengue are often advised to protect themselves more seriously, rather than assuming “I’ve had it, so I won’t get it again”."}}, {"id": "I2ENs7iXOx", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the dengue situation in Thailand in 2026?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "FRWGb3lzaU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At the start of 2026, the Department of Disease Control, Ministry of Public Health, estimated that this year’s outbreak was likely to be worse than last year’s, with possibly around 76,000–80,000 cases and about 76 deaths if mosquito breeding sites were not well controlled."}}, {"id": "npeuAKJ5gT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The latest mid-year data (to 8 July 2026) from the Department of Disease Control showed 13,143 cumulative cases nationwide and 19 deaths — still somewhat lower than the same period in 2025. But dengue usually peaks in the rainy season from June to September, so the numbers are likely to keep rising over the coming months. In Bangkok, Aedes larvae indices are monitored weekly in many areas — another reminder that this is not a disease to ignore."}}, {"id": "Woongs0U_g", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "What is the dengue vaccine, and how well does it work?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "3v7I5x93hJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The vaccine widely used in Thailand is Qdenga, officially TAK-003, made by Takeda. It is a live attenuated vaccine designed to cover all 4 dengue virus types in the same injection. It is given as 2 doses, 3 months apart. Unlike earlier dengue vaccines, Qdenga can be given without a blood test to confirm previous infection, making it much more convenient and accessible."}}, {"id": "BlzG63NPRo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In terms of effectiveness, phase 3 studies following participants in several countries found that Qdenga reduced symptomatic dengue by about 61% and hospitalisation from dengue by about 84% — quite high for this type of vaccine. The World Health Organization (WHO) therefore recommends it for children aged 6–16 in high-transmission areas, and suggests considering it for people aged up to 60 with conditions that put them at risk of severe illness, such as diabetes, kidney disease or heart disease, who live in countries with dengue outbreaks. Its general registration covers people aged 4 and over."}}, {"id": "vt4PUFBt0R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "It is important to understand that the vaccine greatly reduces the risk and severity of dengue, but it is not 100% protective. Getting rid of mosquito breeding sites and preventing bites are still necessary."}}, {"id": "_qTejKfbF7", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Who should get it, and who should take extra care?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "HOLIsiwBGM", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["People who live or work in areas with regular dengue outbreaks, especially Bangkok and the surrounding provinces", "People who have had dengue before, because reinfection carries a higher risk of severe illness", "People with long-term conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure, kidney disease or heart disease, who are at risk of severe illness if infected", "Children aged 4 and over in families concerned about the risk"]}}, {"id": "xtYlC-Nm3z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or have a weakened immune system, always talk to a doctor before deciding, because it is a live vaccine with specific precautions that the doctor must assess case by case."}}, {"id": "GVUs5s0BYY", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Where to get the dengue vaccine, and how much does it cost in 2026?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "ca-efsJHby", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prices for the Qdenga vaccine vary widely between hospitals and clinics in Bangkok, depending on promotions and whether doctor and service fees are included."}}, {"id": "ug76MNmDk7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At HappiWell Medical Clinic in Thung Khru, we aim to make the dengue vaccine easier to access for local people. The price is 1,800 baht per dose (you can pay per dose) or 3,450 baht for the 2-dose course, with a doctor’s consultation before every injection to check it suits your body and health history. It is quick, too — from seeing the doctor to finishing your injection takes no more than 15 minutes. No need to travel to a big hospital; booking is easy and the wait is short."}}, {"id": "wMWJVsxr78", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To book your dengue vaccine, message us on LINE or call HappiWell Clinic. dengue-signs-in-children-rainy-season.content: {"time": 1785466695186, "blocks": [{"id": "Gs70ZkQg3J", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Why be especially careful about dengue in the rainy season?", "level": 2}}, {"id": "QJQ5B7PaeM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, carried by Aedes mosquitoes, which usually lay eggs and breed in standing water in containers around the home. The rainy season, when there is more standing water everywhere, is when dengue outbreaks are especially common — particularly in young children, whose immune systems are not yet fully developed."}}, {"id": "0E4qPp5jPM", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Common early symptoms", "level": 3}}, {"id": "wGDLdzBAnN", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["A sudden high fever of 38.5–40°C lasting several days", "Headache, and aching muscles and bones", "Nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite", "Possibly a red rash on the body", "A flushed face and red eyes"]}}, {"id": "gvjgWZuvKm", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Danger signs: take your child to a doctor immediately", "level": 3}}, {"id": "XXCju9krFW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The time when the fever starts to fall is usually the time to watch most carefully, because symptoms can suddenly get worse. If your child has any of the following, take them to hospital immediately without waiting:"}}, {"id": "6XmveZeYLt", "type": "list", "data": {"style": "unordered", "items": ["Severe stomach pain", "Frequent, persistent vomiting", "Unusual bleeding, such as nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or blood in vomit or stools", "Drowsiness, reduced alertness or unusual restlessness", "Cold skin, cold hands and feet, or heavy sweating", "Passing less urine, or no urine for several hours"]}}, {"id": "T5aheBlczh", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Basic care at home", "level": 3}}, {"id": "2jQ6qrE5rX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you suspect your child may have dengue, sponge them to bring down the fever and give only paracetamol for fever. Do not give aspirin or NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen), as they may increase the risk of bleeding. Give water or oral rehydration solution often, and watch your child closely during the first 3–7 days of the fever. If the fever does not come down or any of the danger signs above appear, bring your child to a doctor immediately — do not wait and watch at home."}}], "version": "2.29.1"}
